````text
# codemap

Ask how your code works and get a map you can point at. Claude explores the repo and drafts the answer as a graph of
areas, steps and labeled arrows. A plain program checks every box and arrow against the real code before you see it.
Then you can take a walkthrough, select any part and ask about it, and fix a missing connection right from the map.

Design: [Codemap v1 Design](https://claude.ai/artifact/55L8tokprGe61qtfpDXJ5h).

## Use it

```
npm i
npm run build                                              # the viewer
npm run codemap -- "What happens when a user signs up?" --repo /path/to/your/repo
```

It prints a link (`http://127.0.0.1:4317/m/<id>?t=<token>`) and opens it. Maps are saved in the target repo under
`.codemap/maps/`; commit them to share. Other commands:

```
npm run codemap -- open --repo <dir>            # maps already made in that repo
npm run codemap -- check <map-id> --repo <dir>  # re-check a saved map against the code (exit 1 if a claim fails)
```

Options: `--port <n>` (default 4317), `--no-open`, `--model <id>` (default `claude-opus-5-5`, or `CODEMAP_MODEL`).

Claude access: an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or a logged-in Claude Code (the Agent SDK uses it).

To put `codemap` on your PATH: `npm link -w @codemap/server`.

### From a coding agent

`integrations/skills/codemap/SKILL.md` is a skill in the standard `SKILL.md` format. Copy the `codemap` folder into
`.claude/skills/` (Claude Code), `.agents/skills/` (Codex, Gemini CLI) or `.cursor/skills/` (Cursor). Your agent then
runs codemap when you ask how something works, and hands you the link.

### Try it without a model

```
npm run preview
```

The real server and viewer on a throwaway copy of the care-app fixture, with a scripted stand-in for Claude. Nothing
is sent anywhere. Useful for UI work and demos.

## How it works

1. **Make a map.** A deterministic scan gives Claude a head start (entry points, routes, which requests hit which
   routes, which tables are written). Claude explores with Read/Grep/Glob only and returns the map in a fixed format.
2. **Check every claim.** `check()` re-reads each cited line, verifies calls, requests and imports against code facts,
   and re-runs the search behind every "nothing does X". Claude gets up to two rounds to fix what didn't hold. Anything
   still unconfirmed is shown with a "?", never hidden.
3. **Explore.** The viewer draws areas, steps, labeled arrows and red dashed gaps, with a walkthrough Claude wrote. Select
   anything and ask: answers come at three depths (concept, how it works, code) with their sources. Claude explores
   further when the map isn't enough; what it finds is drawn only if it passes the checker.
4. **Fix from the map.** Ask for a change and Claude proposes a fix, drawn as a green dashed arrow next to the exact diff.
   Nothing changes until you approve. Then codemap writes exactly that change (refusing if the files changed since),
   re-checks the map, and offers Undo.

## Packages

| Package | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `@codemap/facts` | What the code says, read deterministically: imports, symbols, calls, routes, table reads and writes, fetch → route links. TS/JS via oxc, Python and Go via tree-sitter. Carried over from the hackathon harness with its tests. |
| `@codemap/core` | The map format (`parseMap`), the checker (`check`), map edits, and read-only repo access that never reads secrets. |
| `@codemap/server` | The Claude map maker and explainer (Agent SDK, read-only tools, secret guard), fixes, the local HTTP/WebSocket server, and the `codemap` CLI. |
| `@codemap/viewer` | The React Flow + ELK viewer: the map, walkthrough, answers, fixes and the input bar. |

## Development

```
npm test           # every package (no model calls; Claude is scripted in tests)
npm run typecheck
npm run build      # the viewer bundle the server serves
```

`packages/core/test/fixtures/care-app` is the reference app: staff convert a patient, the app announces it, nothing
listens, so the welcome email never goes out. `care-app.map.json` is the map of that question.
````

````text
# codemap

A map you can point at and ask about, for code you didn't write yourself. Read `README.md`, then `HANDOFF.md` (who it's
for, what users asked for, the decisions and why, what's next, gotchas). The design lives in the "Codemap v1 Design"
artifact (link in both).

## Rules

- **The model writes, the code decides.** Nothing reaches the screen without passing `check()` in `@codemap/core`. A
  model never sets a claim's status; the checker computes it from the repo every time.
- **One checker, every call site.** Publishing a map, every answer, reopening a saved map, and after a fix all call the
  same `check()`. Don't fork its logic.
- **"Nothing does X" is a claim too.** Absences carry the search that proves them, and the checker reruns it.
- **The map format is the one-way door.** Change `packages/core/src/format.ts` deliberately, with tests. Everything
  else (generator, viewer, explainer) is replaceable behind it.
- **Read-only unless approved.** Codemap writes to a target repo only under `.codemap/`, and edits product code only
  after the user approves a fix previewed on the map. Claude never edits: it proposes, and `applyFix` writes exactly
  the approved change, refusing if the files changed since. Only one agent edits at a time.
- **All model calls go through one `Agent`** (`packages/server/src/agent.ts`): read-only tools, the secret guard,
  structured output. Tests inject a scripted `Agent`; `npm test` never calls a model.
- **Never read secrets.** `.env*`, keys and similar files are refused by `createRepoReader` and left out of searches.
  Paths in maps must stay inside the repo.
- **No model calls in `@codemap/facts` or the checker.** They must be deterministic and fast.
- **Plain English in anything a person reads.** Jargon belongs in the code tab and in engineering detail.
- TypeScript strict, with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. Vitest. Pin dependency versions exactly.
- **Don't guess Agent SDK or Claude Code APIs** (channels, MCP Apps, hooks). Check the docs first.

## Commands

```
npm i
npm test             # every package, no model calls
npm run typecheck
npm run build        # viewer bundle (the server serves packages/viewer/dist)
npm run preview      # whole app with a scripted Claude, on a copy of the care-app fixture
npm run codemap -- "<question>" --repo <dir>   # the real thing (uses Claude)
```

## Context

- Packages: `facts` (deterministic code facts) → `core` (format, checker, map edits, safe repo reads) → `server`
  (maker, explainer, fixes, HTTP/WebSocket server, CLI) → `viewer` (React Flow + ELK). The viewer imports server and
  core types only (`import type`), never their runtime code.
- The agent skill is `integrations/skills/codemap/SKILL.md`.
- `@codemap/facts` was carried over from the hackathon harness (`../Speedhacks-project/packages/core`) with its tests.
  The harness is a separate project; don't import from it or edit it from here.
- Test fixtures: `packages/facts/test/{alias-repo,fixture-py,fixture-go}` and `packages/core/test/fixtures/care-app`
  (planted missing listener). Its `.env` holds a fake key for the secret-refusal tests.
----
# Handoff: where codemap came from, what's decided, what's next

Context for anyone (person or agent) picking codemap up. The code and `README.md` say *what* exists; this says *why*,
what was learned along the way, and what's still open. As of 2026-11-02.

## 1. The problem

When you build mostly by directing AI agents, you lose your model of the system. Fixes become band-aids: each change is
judged locally ("did the error go away?") rather than against how the system is meant to work, and nobody notices the
same spot being patched five times. Call it **comprehension debt**: code that exists but that no person understands.

The founding example is real. On an EHR workflow builder (care journeys, journey templates, automations such as "send
this email after the patient converts"), the concepts kept getting rewired, and the frontend looked finished. It was
impossible to tell how the backend was wired, or whether it was wired at all. *"I just trusted what I saw on the
frontend."*

## 2. Who it's for

- **Main user: semi-technical builders who ship with agents.** They know enough to act on what a map shows ("nothing
  listens for this event" is obviously a bug), but can't hold the whole system in their head. This group is growing
  fastest.
- **Not fully non-technical people.** They want "make it work and don't make me think about the backend", which works
  against the product. They're also mostly inside Lovable, Replit or Bolt, which own the screen.
- **Not senior engineers, mostly.** They already hold the model. The exception is an unfamiliar codebase.
- **Buyer later: teams and eng leads** worried about agent-written code nobody understands.
- **Framing:** it's not "leveling the playing field". It's "stay in control of what your agent builds, and get better
  at it as you go."

## 3. What people said (Oct 2026 interviews)

- **Jay** struggles with UX iteration; that's a different product, so leave it out. Separately, he worries whether V1 will
  hold up for V2 and V3, and has no visibility into the backend his technical cofounder owns. That suggests **the map as
  a shared language between a non-technical founder (who views and asks) and a technical cofounder (who acts).**
  Promise "you'll see where V2 will hurt", not "you'll know it scales".
- **The integration interviewee is the clearest signal.** He had to change a client's data integration, asked GPT how
  the workflow worked, and got a wall of text instead of a diagram. *Consultants working in client codebases* may be a
  sharp segment: they hit this on every new client.
- **The third person** plans heavily and says AI implements well "but…". The note cut off. **Follow up**: this is either
  the toughest customer or evidence that the pain is smaller for disciplined planners.
- **The bar to clear is "ask Claude for a Mermaid diagram".** That's free and solves maybe 60% of "wall of text". Codemap
  has to win on things people notice: claims checked against the code, click-through to the code, the same drawing every
  time, and **showing what's missing**.

## 4. What the user wants from the interface (direct feedback)

- **Point at anything and ask.** Select a box, an arrow or a region; answers appear next to what was selected.
- **Plain English first.** Translating code into concepts *is* the value. Three depths: Concept, How it works, Code.
  Define jargon. Use a small concrete example from their own code.
- **A real graph:** areas as containers, steps inside, labeled arrows between them. An early design with lane rows of
  blocks was rejected as "unintuitive, not an actual graph".
- **A walkthrough written with each map,** because a graph alone is hard to start reading. Stops go in the order that
  makes sense to a newcomer, and you can ask at every stop.
- **No "guess what happens next" prompts.** That idea was rejected.
- **The agent can fix things from the map**, not just explain them (see decision 5).
- **Model-agnostic is wanted.** The simplest version: codemap runs its own Claude explainer, and any coding agent
  launches it.
- **Learning from walkthroughs:** a diagram of the user's own vibecoded architecture lost them. Every diagram needs its
  question and a line of context on top, 5 to 7 boxes at first with details on click, and plain labels.

## 5. Design decisions and why

1. **v1: Claude explores, a plain program checks.** No deterministic graph engine yet, because it isn't needed for
   "ask, get a map". Claude explores with Read/Grep/Glob and returns the map in a fixed format. `check()` re-reads every
   cited line and verifies calls, requests and imports against code facts. Later, the engine can replace the explorer
   behind the same format.
2. **The map format (`packages/core/src/format.ts`) is the one-way door.** Everything else is replaceable. Statuses are
   never stored; they're computed on every check.
3. **"Nothing does X" is a claim with proof.** Absences carry the search that proves them, and the checker reruns it.
   The missing connection is the bug people care about, and only a graph that can show absences can show it.
4. **Codemap runs its own Claude explainer,** separate from the user's coding chat. It works with any agent and keeps
   explanation quality consistent. It can read the whole repo: the map is a starting point, not a fence. Anything it
   adds is drawn only if the checker confirms it.
5. **Fixes:** Claude proposes. The fix is drawn as a green dashed arrow next to the exact diff. Nothing changes until
   approval. Then codemap writes exactly that diff, refusing if the files changed since the proposal, re-checks the map,
   and offers Undo. Only one agent edits at a time. If codemap is ever connected to the user's coding chat, that agent
   makes the edit instead.
6. **Delivery:** the basic version works everywhere through a skill, the `codemap` CLI and a browser tab. Optional
   upgrades (not built):
   - **Channels:** Claude Code only, research preview. An MCP server pushes the user's question into the running chat.
   - **MCP Apps:** Cursor, VS Code Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude Desktop. The viewer embeds in the chat, and `ui/message` sends
     questions.
   - **Codex:** no documented way to push into a running session. Its desktop app has a Browser with an Annotate picker
     and WebMCP, which might allow something similar; untested.
7. **Local only:** binds to 127.0.0.1, a token is required, Host and Origin are checked, and secrets are never read.

## 6. Graphify, for comparison (github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify, read at v0.9.97)

- **Agent-facing.** Code goes to a graph through tree-sitter (no LLM). Query is keyword match, then BFS spreading in every
  direction. Clusters (Leiden) are named after their busiest node. Updates happen after commits, asynchronously, in
  seconds. There are no ordered flows, no fetch → route links, and no events or queues for JS. Its "benchmark" measures
  tokens, not task success. Graphify Cloud (YC S26) adds architecture rules.
- **Ideas worth borrowing:**
  - An edge counts as EXTRACTED only with import evidence; ambiguous matches are dropped rather than guessed.
  - Edges belong to the file they come from, so a change evicts only that file's edges.
  - Keep cluster IDs stable between rebuilds.
  - Stamp the graph with `built_at_commit`.
  - Hook messages phrased as facts, not commands. They found imperative wording gets ignored as prompt injection.
- **Don't build on it.** Codemap's edge is everything it lacks.

## 7. What's built (verified)

- **Tests:** four packages, 102 tests, no model calls.
- **Viewer:** tested in Chrome with scripted Claude (`npm run preview`): making a map, the walkthrough, select and ask,
  a follow-up that adds checked steps, a fix (approve, reload, undo).
- **Real Claude, on the care-app fixture:**
  - The map came back 20 of 20 confirmed on the first pass, for about $0.21.
  - It also found a bug nobody planted: nothing ever starts the nightly job.
  - A real question cost about $0.14 and added two confirmed gaps.
  - A real fix cost about $0.24, was approved and applied, and re-checked 22 of 22.
- **Demo frontend:** `examples/care-app-ui/index.html`, the patient app as staff see it. Convert a patient and no welcome
  email arrives, even though the automation is active.

## 8. Not built yet, and next steps

- **Questions, answers and fix proposals live in server memory** and are lost on restart; maps are saved to disk.
- **Hand-off to the user's coding agent** (channels / MCP Apps) and an MCP `publish_map` tool for agents that explore on
  their own.
- **Big repos are untested.** The head-start scan reads the whole repo.
- **Next, in order:**
  1. **Run Phase 0 with the integration interviewee:** his real question, codemap vs "Claude + Mermaid" side by side.
  2. Try codemap on a real repo, or a fresh Scout copy (`../scout-run`; never `../scout-agent`).
  3. Persist sessions.
  4. Channels hand-off in Claude Code.
  5. MCP Apps.
- **Later (Phase 3 of the plan):**
  - A fast graph engine with updates on every edit (incremental, LSP-style).
  - Live agent activity on the map.
  - "Working somewhere you haven't explored" and a per-user explored-regions map.
  - "This step was patched 5 times this week" counters. That's the *band-aid detector*, and it needs a time dimension.

## 9. Gotchas that cost time

- **Agent SDK (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.296), verified from its types:**
  - The call is `query({ prompt, options: { cwd, model, tools, allowedTools, permissionMode: 'dontAsk', settingSources: [], strictMcpConfig, outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema }, resume, hooks } })`.
  - The answer arrives as `structured_output` on the `result` message.
  - PreToolUse hooks can return `permissionDecision` and `updatedInput`.
  - Auth is an API key or the Claude Code login.
- **React Flow 12:**
  - With controlled nodes, measurements live on `getInternalNode(id).measured`, not on your node objects.
  - Nodes that aren't selectable or draggable get `pointer-events: none` unless `onNodeClick` is set. Steps carry
    `nopan` so a pan doesn't swallow clicks.
- **ELK:** spacing options apply per container, so each area repeats them.
- **Chrome automation:**
  - A hidden tab renders no React Flow edges and drops input; check `document.visibilityState` and drive the page with
    in-page events.
  - The first click after a navigation is often dropped.
- **zsh `echo` mangles backslashes in JSON.** Write curl output to a file instead.
- **Channels with a custom server:**
  - Launch with `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:<name>`.
  - Claude Code won't register a channel server on MCP protocol 2026-07-28; `MCP_SDK_GENERATION=v1` works around it.
  - The page needs its own sender check (a token): an ungated channel is a prompt-injection risk.

## 10. Links

- Design spec, current: [Codemap v1 Design](https://claude.ai/artifact/55L8tokprGe61qtfpDXJ5h)
- Longer-term plan with the engine: [Point-and-Ask Architecture](https://claude.ai/artifact/7hWiwFyugpB6hT6x3DKoJs)
- Graphify vs. ours: [Two Code Graphs Compared](https://claude.ai/artifact/8u9v9BAXW4pTLkz72exhv5)
- Early concept frames (Figma): https://www.figma.com/design/i8aTiDS47Eb68QeoKvQopW
- Hackathon origin, reference only: `../Speedhacks-project` (the Interpretability harness)
- Claude Code channels: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels · MCP Apps client matrix:
  https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/client-matrix
````

```text
/** A fake agent that replies from a script, in order, and records every request. */
export function scriptedAgent(replies: ((req: AgentRequest) => unknown)[]): Agent & { calls: AgentRequest[] } {
  const calls: AgentRequest[] = [];
  const agent = (async (req: AgentRequest): Promise<AgentResponse> => {
    calls.push(req);
    const reply = replies[calls.length - 1];
    if (!reply) throw new Error(`no scripted reply for call ${calls.length}`);
    req.onProgress?.({ kind: 'read', text: 'Reading src/patients/service.ts' });
    return { output: reply(req), sessionId: `session-${calls.length}`, cost: 0.01 };
  }) as Agent & { calls: AgentRequest[] };
  agent.calls = calls;
  return agent;
}
```

```text
const withQuestion = (output: unknown, question: string) =>
  output && typeof output === 'object' ? { ...(output as Record<string, unknown>), version: 1, question } : output;

export async function makeMap(o: MakeOptions): Promise<MakeResult> {
  const status = (text: string) => o.onProgress?.({ kind: 'status', text });
  status('Scanning the code for ways in, routes and tables');
  const hints = await headStart(o.root);
  status('Claude is exploring the code');
  const run = (prompt: string, resume: string | null) =>
    o.agent({ prompt, schema: MAP_SCHEMA, cwd: o.root, resume, model: o.model, onProgress: o.onProgress, signal: o.signal });

  let res = await run(makerPrompt(o.question, hints.text), null);
  let cost = res.cost ?? 0;
  let rounds = 1;
  let best: { map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport } | null = null;
  let lastProblems: string[] = [];

  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    const parsed = parseMap(withQuestion(res.output, o.question));
    let repair: string | null = null;
    if (!parsed.ok) {
      lastProblems = parsed.problems;
      repair = shapeRepairPrompt(parsed.problems);
    } else {
      status('Checking every claim against the code');
      const report = check(parsed.map, o.root);
      if (!best || report.summary.unconfirmed < best.report.summary.unconfirmed) best = { map: parsed.map, report };
      status(`${report.summary.confirmed} of ${report.summary.claims} claims confirmed`);
      if (report.summary.unconfirmed > 0) repair = evidenceRepairPrompt(report);
    }
    if (!repair || attempt >= (o.repairs ?? 2)) break;
    status(parsed.ok ? 'Asking Claude to fix the claims that didn\'t check out' : 'Asking Claude to fix the map\'s structure');
    res = await run(repair, res.sessionId);
    cost += res.cost ?? 0;
    rounds++;
  }
  if (!best) throw new Error(`Claude's map couldn't be read: ${lastProblems.slice(0, 5).join('; ')}`);
  return { ...best, sessionId: res.sessionId, cost, rounds };
}
```

````bash
## How the pieces fit

- **Make** (`server/src/maker.ts`): `headStart` (a `@codemap/facts` scan, `hints.ts`) seeds the prompt → `Agent` returns
  JSON against `MAP_SCHEMA` → `parseMap` → `check`. Shape errors or unconfirmed claims get up to two repair rounds on
  the same session; the best-checked map wins. Prompts live in `prompts.ts`, output schemas in `schemas.ts`.
- **Ask** (`explainer.ts`): answers may carry additions (merged with `addToMap` in `core/src/edit.ts`) and a fix.
  Additions that don't pass `check` are dropped before the map is returned, not shown as unconfirmed.
- **Fix** (`fixes.ts`): `proposeFix` records file hashes → `applyFix` writes only if they still match →
  `connectAfterFix` draws the new edge and closes the gaps it fills → `undoFix`.
- **Serve** (`server.ts`, `store.ts`): maps persist as `<repo>/.codemap/maps/<id>.json`; jobs, answers and fix
  proposals are in memory only. Binds 127.0.0.1, requires a token, checks Host and Origin; the viewer gets job
  progress over the WebSocket.
- Server tests use `scriptedAgent` and `copyCareApp` from `packages/server/test/helpers.ts`; follow that pattern
````

```text
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## codemap

A map you can point at and ask about, for code you didn't write yourself. Read `README.md`, then `HANDOFF.md` (who it's
for, what users asked for, the decisions and why, what's next, gotchas). The design lives in the "Codemap v1 Design"
artifact (link in both).

## Rules

- **The model writes, the code decides.** Nothing reaches the screen without passing `check()` in `@codemap/core`. A
  model never sets a claim's status; the checker computes it from the repo every time.
- **One checker, every call site.** Publishing a map, every answer, reopening a saved map, and after a fix all call the
  same `check()`. Don't fork its logic.
- **"Nothing does X" is a claim too.** Absences carry the search that proves them, and the checker reruns it.
- **The map format is the one-way door.** Change `packages/core/src/format.ts` deliberately, with tests. Everything
  else (generator, viewer, explainer) is replaceable behind it.
- **Read-only unless approved.** Codemap writes to a target repo only under `.codemap/`, and edits product code only
```

- **Two easy-to-miss facts:**
  - Only the viewer gets built. The other packages run straight from their TypeScript source, so after changing the viewer you need `npm run build` before `npm run codemap`. `preview` rebuilds for you.
  - Vitest only finds tests named `test/*.test.ts` directly in each package's `test/` folder, not in subfolders.
- **A new "How the pieces fit" section:**
  - **Make:** the code scan's head start, then Claude, then the format check and `check()`, with up to two repair rounds; the map with the most confirmed claims wins.
  - **Ask:** anything Claude adds to the map that fails `check()` is dropped, not shown with a "?".
  - **Fix:** propose → apply (only if the files haven't changed) → draw the new connection → undo.
  - **Serve:** maps are saved to disk, while jobs, answers and fix proposals live only in server memory.
  - **Tests:** server tests use the scripted Claude helpers in `packages/server/test/helpers.ts`.

I left out what `HANDOFF.md` already covers (the Agent SDK, React Flow and ELK gotchas), since `CLAUDE.md` already points to it.

There are no Cursor, Copilot, Codex or Gemini config files in the repo, so there was nothing to import.

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... npm run codemap -- "How does signup work?" --repo /path/to/repo
```

```
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
```

**Or skip the key entirely.** If you're logged into Claude Code on this machine, the SDK uses that login, so `npm run codemap -- ...` works as is.

```mjs
}

register();
await import('../src/cli.ts');
```

````text
# codemap

codemap turns a question about this repo into a map the person can explore in their browser: areas of the app, the
steps in order, labeled arrows, and red dashed arrows where something that should be connected isn't. A plain program
checks every claim against the code before it's shown. In the map they can take a walkthrough, select any box or arrow
and ask about it, and approve fixes that codemap applies and re-checks.

## When to use it

- The user asks how something works across several files: "what happens when…", "how does X reach Y", "where does Z
  get triggered".
- The user is about to change code they don't understand yet and wants to see it first.
- The user asks for a map, diagram, graph or walkthrough of part of the code.

Don't use it for a question about a single line or function; answer that directly.

## How to run it

Run from the repo root (or pass `--repo`). Use the user's question in their own words:

```bash
codemap "What happens when a patient converts?" --repo "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
```

It starts a small local server, explores the code with Claude (about a minute for a small repo), and prints a link
like `http://127.0.0.1:4317/m/<id>?t=<token>`. Give the user that link and tell them to open it. The command keeps
running to serve the map: run it in the background, and don't wait for it to exit.

Other commands:

- `codemap open` lists the maps already made in this repo (they're saved under `.codemap/maps/`).
- `codemap check <map-id>` re-checks a saved map against the current code and prints anything that no longer holds.
  It exits with 1 if a claim fails, so it can run in CI.

## Notes

- codemap reads the code and never changes it, except for a fix the user approves in the map.
- It never reads secret files (`.env`, keys) and only listens on 127.0.0.1.
- It needs Claude access: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or a logged-in Claude Code.
- If `codemap` isn't on the PATH, it hasn't been installed. Tell the user to install it from the codemap repo
  (see its README) instead of guessing another command.
````

**To set it up for every project on this machine:**

```
cd /Users/johnzhang/Documents/GitHub/codemap

```

A link is better than a copy, because later edits to the skill take effect without reinstalling. Your `.env` key still works when `codemap` is run from another project, because the launcher finds the `.env` in this folder.

**How to trigger it**, in Claude Code in any project:
- **Just ask** how something works across several files, for example "what happens when a user signs up?" or "how does billing connect to accounts?". Claude picks the skill from its description, runs `codemap` in the background and gives you the link. For a question about a single function, it answers directly instead.
- **Or call it by name:** `/codemap what happens when a user signs up?`
- **Or skip the agent:** `codemap "your question" --repo .` in a terminal.

Skills load when a session starts, so restart any open Claude Code sessions after installing.

Want me to run the two setup commands? They only change your machine, not this repo, and you can undo them with `npm unlink` and by deleting the link in `~/.claude/skills/codemap`.

## How codemap turns a question into a diagram, per its own map

Claude drew it in four areas:

**1. Asking a question.** There are two ways in: the `codemap "<question>"` command (`cli.ts:85`) or the start page in the browser (`home.tsx:22`, which sends `POST /api/maps`). Both reach `startMap` on the local server (`server.ts:93`). It gives the question an id and runs the work in the background, so the page can show live progress.

**2. Making the map.** `makeMap` (`maker.ts`) works in three steps:
- **Head start:** a quick scan with no AI involved (`hints.ts:14`) finds landmarks such as entry points, routes, which requests hit which routes, and which tables get written.
- **Ask Claude:** the one `Agent` (`agent.ts:60`) runs Claude with read-only tools. Claude returns a draft map in the fixed JSON format.
- **Repair loop:** if the draft fails the checks in step 3, Claude gets the list of problems and tries again, up to two more times. The attempt with the most confirmed claims wins.

**3. Checking against the code.** Each draft goes through two gates:
- `parseMap` (`format.ts:103`) checks the shape.
- `check()` (`check.ts:47`) opens every cited file, confirms the quoted line and the kind of arrow, and re-runs the search behind each "nothing does X" to make sure it still finds nothing.

The map's one red dashed "nothing does X" is a feature, not a bug. It says the checker never calls Claude, backed by a search for the Agent SDK in `packages/core/src/**` that finds nothing. In other words, a map can't vouch for itself.

**4. Showing the map.**
- The best attempt is saved to `.codemap/maps/<id>.json` (`store.ts:52`).
- `publishMap` (`server.ts:86`) checks it again against the current code and sends it to the browser over the WebSocket.
- The viewer's state code (`state.ts:149`) switches to the diagram. Anything still unconfirmed shows with a "?".

That matches what I found reading the code earlier. One thing the map left out: answering a question about a selected part, and fixes, both go through the same `check()` afterwards. Those are separate flows from making the first map.

## Worth knowing from this run
- **It cost $1.22**, about six times the $0.21 for the small test project, and took about two minutes. Codemap is much bigger than that project, so this is an early sign of the large-repo cost that `HANDOFF.md` lists as untested.
- `.codemap/` is gitignored in this repo, so the map stays local.
- The server keeps running until you stop it. In the map you can take the walkthrough or select any box and ask about it.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/johnzhang/.claude/skills/codemap

# codemap

codemap turns a question about this repo into a map the person can explore in their browser: areas of the app, the
steps in order, labeled arrows, and red dashed arrows where something that should be connected isn't. A plain program
checks every claim against the code before it's shown. In the map they can take a walkthrough, select any box or arrow
and ask about it, and approve fixes that codemap applies and re-checks.

## When to use it

- The user asks how something works across several files: "what happens when…", "how does X reach Y", "where does Z
  get triggered".
- The user is about to change code they don't understand yet and wants to see it first.
- The user asks for a map, diagram, graph or walkthrough of part of the code.

Don't use it for a question about a single line or function; answer that directly.

## How to run it

Run from the repo root (or pass `--repo`). Use the user's question in their own words:

```bash
codemap "What happens when a patient converts?" --repo "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
```

It starts a small local server, explores the code with Claude (about a minute for a small repo), and prints a link
like `http://127.0.0.1:4317/m/<id>?t=<token>`. Give the user that link and tell them to open it. The command keeps
running to serve the map: run it in the background, and don't wait for it to exit.

Other commands:

- `codemap open` lists the maps already made in this repo (they're saved under `.codemap/maps/`).
- `codemap check <map-id>` re-checks a saved map against the current code and prints anything that no longer holds.
  It exits with 1 if a claim fails, so it can run in CI.

## Notes

- codemap reads the code and never changes it, except for a fix the user approves in the map.
- It never reads secret files (`.env`, keys) and only listens on 127.0.0.1.
- It needs Claude access: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or a logged-in Claude Code.
- If `codemap` isn't on the PATH, it hasn't been installed. Tell the user to install it from the codemap repo
  (see its README) instead of guessing another command.

```text
// The checker: decides which claims in a map the code actually backs. It reads the repo and never writes. One function,
// used everywhere a map reaches a person: when it's published, on every answer, when a saved map is reopened, after a fix.
// No model calls. Python and Go facts need `initTreeSitter()` to have been awaited once; TS/JS needs nothing.
import {
  DEFAULT_IGNORE,
  createFactsIndex,
  fileExistsIn,
  findFetchSites,
  listRepoFiles,
  matchRoute,
  matchesAny,
  settleCalls,
  squash,
  symbolNames,
  type CallFact,
  type FileFacts,
} from '@codemap/facts';
import type { CodeMap, Evidence, MapAbsence, MapEdge, MapNode } from './format';
import { createRepoReader, isSecretPath, type RepoReader } from './repo';

export type Status = 'confirmed' | 'unconfirmed';
/** `fact`: the extracted code facts back the claim. `text`: the cited lines say what the claim says. */
export type Proof = 'fact' | 'text';
export type EvidenceCheck = { file: string; line: number; ok: boolean; foundAt: number | null; reason: string | null };
export type ClaimCheck = { status: Status; proof: Proof | null; evidence: EvidenceCheck[]; reasons: string[] };
export type AbsenceCheck = { status: Status; found: number; locations: { file: string; line: number }[]; reasons: string[] };
export type TourCheck = { status: 'ok' | 'mentions-unconfirmed'; unconfirmed: string[] };
export type CheckReport = {
  nodes: Record<string, ClaimCheck>;
  edges: Record<string, ClaimCheck>;
  absences: Record<string, AbsenceCheck>;
  tour: Record<string, TourCheck>;
  summary: { claims: number; confirmed: number; unconfirmed: number };
};
export type CheckOptions = {
  /** Extra globs to leave out of searches (build output and `.codemap/` are always left out). */
  ignore?: readonly string[];
  /** How far a cited line may have moved and still count (default 3). */
  lineWindow?: number;
};

const MAX_LOCATIONS = 20;
const fileOf = (symbol: string) => symbol.slice(0, symbol.indexOf('#'));
const within = (from: string, symbol: string) => from === symbol || from.startsWith(`${symbol}.`);
const short = (text: string) => (text.length > 60 ? `${text.slice(0, 57)}…` : text);

export function check(map: CodeMap, root: string, options: CheckOptions = {}): CheckReport {
  const repo = createRepoReader(root);
  const window = options.lineWindow ?? 3;
  const facts = factsFor(repo);
  const byId = new Map(map.nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n]));
  let repoFiles: string[] | null = null;
  const files = () => (repoFiles ??= listRepoFiles(repo.root, [...DEFAULT_IGNORE, ...(options.ignore ?? [])]).filter((f) => !isSecretPath(f)));

  const nodes: Record<string, ClaimCheck> = {};
  for (const n of map.nodes) nodes[n.id] = checkNode(n, repo, facts, window);
  const edges: Record<string, ClaimCheck> = {};
  for (const e of map.edges) edges[e.id] = checkEdge(e, byId, repo, facts, window);
  const absences: Record<string, AbsenceCheck> = {};
  for (const a of map.absences) absences[a.id] = checkAbsence(a, repo, files());

  const tour: Record<string, TourCheck> = {};
  for (const t of map.tour) {
    const unconfirmed = [
      ...(t.focus.nodes ?? []).filter((id) => nodes[id]?.status !== 'confirmed'),
      ...(t.focus.edges ?? []).filter((id) => edges[id]?.status !== 'confirmed'),
      ...(t.focus.absences ?? []).filter((id) => absences[id]?.status !== 'confirmed'),
    ];
    tour[t.id] = { status: unconfirmed.length ? 'mentions-unconfirmed' : 'ok', unconfirmed };
  }

  const all = [...Object.values(nodes), ...Object.values(edges), ...Object.values(absences)];
  const confirmed = all.filter((c) => c.status === 'confirmed').length;
  return { nodes, edges, absences, tour, summary: { claims: all.length, confirmed, unconfirmed: all.length - confirmed } };
}

/** Facts per file, extracted on demand and cached for one check. */
function factsFor(repo: RepoReader) {
  const index = createFactsIndex(repo.root, fileExistsIn(repo.root), repo.text);
  const cache = new Map<string, FileFacts | null>();
  const get = (file: string): FileFacts | null => {
    if (!cache.has(file)) {
      const text = repo.text(file);
      cache.set(file, text === null ? null : index.extract(file, text).facts);
    }
    return cache.get(file) ?? null;
  };
  return {
    get,
    /** Calls made in `file`, settled against the symbols of `file` and `others`. */
    calls(file: string, others: readonly string[]): CallFact[] {
      const own = get(file);
      if (!own) return [];
      const known: Record<string, FileFacts> = {};
      for (const p of [file, ...others]) {
        const f = get(p);
        if (f) known[p] = f;
      }
      return settleCalls(own.calls, symbolNames(known));
    },
  };
}
type Facts = ReturnType<typeof factsFor>;

function checkEvidence(repo: RepoReader, e: Evidence, window: number): EvidenceCheck {
  const base = { file: e.file, line: e.line };
  const read = repo.read(e.file);
  if (!read.ok) return { ...base, ok: false, foundAt: null, reason: read.reason };
  const lines = read.text.split('\n');
  const want = squash(e.text);
  for (let d = 0; d <= window; d++) {
    for (const at of d === 0 ? [e.line] : [e.line - d, e.line + d]) {
      const line = lines[at - 1];
      if (line !== undefined && squash(line).includes(want)) return { ...base, ok: true, foundAt: at, reason: null };
    }
  }
  // Code moves (a fix above it, a new import). Text that appears on exactly one line of the file is still that line.
  const hits = lines.flatMap((line, i) => (squash(line).includes(want) ? [i + 1] : []));
  if (hits.length === 1) return { ...base, ok: true, foundAt: hits[0]!, reason: null };
  const reason =
    hits.length > 1
      ? `"${short(e.text)}" isn't on line ${e.line} or near it, and appears ${hits.length} times elsewhere in the file`
      : e.line > lines.length
        ? `the file has only ${lines.length} lines`
        : `"${short(e.text)}" isn't on line ${e.line} or near it`;
  return { ...base, ok: false, foundAt: null, reason };
}

function evidenceReasons(evidence: readonly EvidenceCheck[]): string[] {
  return evidence.filter((x) => !x.ok).map((x) => `${x.file}:${x.line}: ${x.reason}`);
}

function result(evidence: EvidenceCheck[], reasons: string[], proof: Proof): ClaimCheck {
  return reasons.length ? { status: 'unconfirmed', proof: null, evidence, reasons } : { status: 'confirmed', proof, evidence, reasons };
}

function checkNode(n: MapNode, repo: RepoReader, facts: Facts, window: number): ClaimCheck {
  const evidence = n.evidence.map((e) => checkEvidence(repo, e, window));
  const reasons = evidenceReasons(evidence);
  if (reasons.length || !n.symbol) return result(evidence, reasons, 'text');

// their head. Plain English first; code names belong in the "code" depth.

const EVIDENCE_RULES = [
  '## Evidence rules (a program checks every claim; anything it can\'t confirm is shown as unconfirmed)',
  '- Every box and arrow cites at least one line: `file` (repo-relative), `line` (1-based), and `text` copied exactly from that line. A distinctive fragment of 10–80 characters works best.',
  '- A box that is a function or method gets `symbol`: "<file>#<name>" (methods as Class.method, object members as obj.member, e.g. "src/db.ts#db.update").',
  '- Arrow `kind`: `calls` when a function in the from box literally calls the function in the to box; `request` when an HTTP call in the from box hits a route handled by the to box; `imports`; `then` for anything else (events, ordering). The checker verifies calls, request and imports against the code, so use them only when literally true.',
  '- Never cite or read secret files (.env, keys).',
];

const MAP_RULES = [
  '## What a good map is',
  '- It follows what happens, in order, from where it starts (a button, a route, a job, a command) to where it ends (a table write, an email, an outside API), or to where it stops.',
  '- 2–6 `areas` named in product language (Patients, Billing, Background jobs), not folder names.',
  '- 4–12 boxes (`nodes`). Each is one step a person would recognize. `name`: plain English, at most 30 characters ("Patient marked enrolled", not "markConverted()").',
  '- `kind`: entry (a way in), step, store (table, queue, cache), external (outside service), job (scheduled or background work).',
  '- `explain` for every box: `concept` (1–2 plain sentences, no jargon), `how` (the mechanism; define any term you use), `code` (function and file names).',
  '- Arrow `label`: 1–3 words saying how one step leads to the next ("sends request", "calls", "announces", "every night").',
  '- When the trail stops, or something that should be connected isn\'t, record an `absence`: the `claim` in plain words, the two boxes it should connect (`between`), and the exact `search` that proves nothing is there (`pattern`, `regex`, optional `paths` globs), with `matches` set to the count that search returns (usually 0). Run that search yourself with Grep first.',
  '- Code that exists but isn\'t reached from the start can still be boxes. Don\'t draw arrows that don\'t exist; use an absence.',
];

const TOUR_RULES = [
  '## Walkthrough (`tour`, written last)',
  '- 4–7 stops in the order a newcomer should read them: what the map shows → the path → the problem, if there is one → what it means.',
  '- Each stop: `title`, `text` (2–3 plain sentences), `focus` (ids of the areas, nodes, edges or absences it\'s about), optional `terms` it uses that need defining, and `ask` with 1–2 good next questions.',
  '- Point stops only at boxes, arrows and absences you\'re confident in.',
];

export function makerPrompt(question: string, headStart: string): string {
  return [
    'You make a map that answers a question about this codebase, for someone semi-technical. Explore with Read, Grep and Glob, then return the map as JSON. You cannot edit anything.',
    '',
    `## The question\n"${question}"`,
    '',
    ...MAP_RULES,
    '',
    ...EVIDENCE_RULES,
    '',
    ...TOUR_RULES,
    '',
    '## Head start (from a quick automatic scan; it may be incomplete)',
    headStart,
    '',
    'Return the map: `version` 1, the `question`, `areas`, `nodes`, `edges`, `absences`, `tour`.',
  ].join('\n');
}

export function shapeRepairPrompt(problems: readonly string[]): string {
  return [
    'The map you returned has problems that stop it from being drawn:',
    ...problems.map((p) => `- ${p}`),
    '',
    'Return the complete corrected map.',
  ].join('\n');
}

export function evidenceRepairPrompt(report: CheckReport): string {
  const lines = [
    ...Object.entries(report.nodes).filter(([, c]) => c.status !== 'confirmed').map(([id, c]) => `- box ${id}: ${c.reasons.join('; ')}`),
    ...Object.entries(report.edges).filter(([, c]) => c.status !== 'confirmed').map(([id, c]) => `- arrow ${id}: ${c.reasons.join('; ')}`),
    ...Object.entries(report.absences).filter(([, c]) => c.status !== 'confirmed').map(([id, c]) => `- absence ${id}: ${c.reasons.join('; ')}${c.locations.length ? ` (found at ${c.locations.slice(0, 5).map((l) => `${l.file}:${l.line}`).join(', ')})` : ''}`),
  ];
  return [
    'The checker re-read the code and could not confirm these claims:',
    ...lines,
    '',
    'For each one: fix the citation (exact line text, right line number, real symbol name, right arrow kind), or remove the claim if it isn\'t true. If an absence was wrong, the code is connected after all: draw that connection instead. Keep everything that was confirmed. Return the complete corrected map.',
  ].join('\n');
}

export type SelectionLine = { id: string; label: string };

export function explainerPrompt(map: CodeMap, report: CheckReport, selection: readonly SelectionLine[], question: string): string {
  const unconfirmed = [
    ...Object.entries(report.nodes), ...Object.entries(report.edges), ...Object.entries(report.absences),
  ].filter(([, c]) => c.status !== 'confirmed').map(([id]) => id);
  return [
    'You answer questions about a code map for someone semi-technical. You can Read, Grep and Glob the repo; you cannot edit anything.',
    '',
    '## The map (JSON)',
    JSON.stringify(map),
    unconfirmed.length ? `\nThe checker could not confirm: ${unconfirmed.join(', ')}. Don\'t rely on those without checking.` : '\nThe checker confirmed every claim in the map.',
    '',
    selection.length ? `## They selected\n${selection.map((s) => `- ${s.id}: ${s.label}`).join('\n')}` : '## They selected nothing (the question is about the whole map)',
    '',
    `## Their question\n"${question}"`,
    '',
    '## How to answer',
    '- `concept`: 2–4 plain sentences, no jargon. `how`: the mechanism; define any term you use. `code`: function names, files and lines.',
    '- `refs`: ids of the boxes, arrows and absences your answer relies on.',
    '- If the map doesn\'t cover it, explore, then put what you found in `add` (new areas, nodes, edges or absences with evidence, same rules as the map; ids must be new). Connect new boxes to existing ones with arrows where the code really connects them.',
    '- `moves`: `focus` on the most relevant id; `highlight` the ids that make up the path that answers the question.',
    '- If they ask for a change, don\'t edit (you can\'t). Propose a `fix`: codemap shows it to them on the map, and if they approve, codemap applies exactly your edits and re-checks the map. So describe it as a proposal waiting for their approval, never as something for them to apply by hand.',
    '- The `fix`: `summary` in plain words; `edits` as exact replacements (`find` copied exactly from the file, occurring once; `replace` is the new text); `creates` for new files. If the fix creates a connection between two boxes, fill `connects` with `from`, `to`, a short `label`, and `evidenceFile` + `evidenceText` (text that will appear in the new code). Keep fixes small and in the style of the surrounding code.',
    '- `followUps`: up to 3 short next questions.',
    '',
    ...EVIDENCE_RULES,
  ].join('\n');
}
// The one place codemap talks to a model: a read-only Claude Agent SDK session that returns structured output.
// Read, Grep and Glob only; secret files are refused and left out of searches. Tests swap in a fake `Agent`.
import * as path from 'node:path';
import { query, type HookCallback, type PreToolUseHookInput } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
import { isSecretPath } from '@codemap/core';

export type Progress = { kind: 'read' | 'search' | 'list'; text: string };

export type AgentRequest = {
  prompt: string;
  schema: Record<string, unknown>;
  cwd: string;
  /** Continue an earlier session (follow-up questions keep what was already read). */
  resume?: string | null;
  model?: string;
  maxTurns?: number;
  onProgress?: (p: Progress) => void;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
};
export type AgentResponse = { output: unknown; sessionId: string | null; cost: number | null };
export type Agent = (req: AgentRequest) => Promise<AgentResponse>;

export const DEFAULT_MODEL = process.env.CODEMAP_MODEL ?? 'claude-opus-5-5';
const READ_ONLY = ['Read', 'Grep', 'Glob'];
/** ripgrep glob that leaves secret files out of a search the model didn't scope itself. */
const NOT_SECRETS = '!**/{.env,.env.*,*.pem,*.key,*.p12,id_rsa*,id_ed25519*,.npmrc,.netrc}';

/** A plain-English progress line for a tool call, with paths relative to the repo. */
export function progressOf(name: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, cwd: string): Progress | null {
  const rel = (p: unknown) => (typeof p === 'string' ? path.relative(cwd, path.resolve(cwd, p)) || '.' : '');
  if (name === 'Read') return { kind: 'read', text: `Reading ${rel(input.file_path)}` };
  if (name === 'Grep') return { kind: 'search', text: `Searching for "${String(input.pattern ?? '')}"${input.path ? ` in ${rel(input.path)}` : ''}` };
  if (name === 'Glob') return { kind: 'list', text: `Looking for files matching ${String(input.pattern ?? '')}` };
  return null;
}

/** Refuse secret files, and keep repo-wide searches away from them. */
export function secretGuard(cwd: string): HookCallback {
  return async (input) => {
    const i = input as PreToolUseHookInput;
    const ti = (i.tool_input ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
    const target = typeof ti.file_path === 'string' ? ti.file_path : typeof ti.path === 'string' ? ti.path : null;
    const rel = target ? path.relative(cwd, path.resolve(cwd, target)) : null;
    if (rel && (rel.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(rel))) {
      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: 'Only files inside this repo can be read.' } };
    }
    if (rel && isSecretPath(rel)) {
      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: 'Secret files are never read.' } };
    }
    if (i.tool_name === 'Grep' && ti.glob === undefined && ti.type === undefined) {
      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'allow', updatedInput: { ...ti, glob: NOT_SECRETS } } };
    }
    return {};
  };
}

export const sdkAgent: Agent = async (req) => {
  const abortController = new AbortController();
  req.signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => abortController.abort(), { once: true });
  const q = query({
    prompt: req.prompt,
    options: {
      cwd: req.cwd,
      model: req.model ?? DEFAULT_MODEL,
      tools: READ_ONLY,
      allowedTools: READ_ONLY,
      permissionMode: 'dontAsk',
      settingSources: [],
      strictMcpConfig: true,
      outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema: req.schema },
      maxTurns: req.maxTurns ?? 60,
      abortController,
      hooks: { PreToolUse: [{ matcher: 'Read|Grep|Glob', hooks: [secretGuard(req.cwd)] }] },
      ...(req.resume ? { resume: req.resume } : {}),
    },
  });
  let sessionId: string | null = null;
  for await (const m of q) {
    if ('session_id' in m && typeof m.session_id === 'string') sessionId = m.session_id;
    if (m.type === 'assistant' && !m.parent_tool_use_id) {
      for (const block of m.message.content) {
        if (block.type !== 'tool_use') continue;
        const p = progressOf(block.name, (block.input ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>, req.cwd);
        if (p) req.onProgress?.(p);
      }
    }
    if (m.type === 'result') {
      if (m.subtype !== 'success' || m.structured_output === undefined) {
        throw Object.assign(new Error(`Claude stopped before answering (${m.subtype}).`), { cost: m.total_cost_usd });
      }
      return { output: m.structured_output, sessionId, cost: m.total_cost_usd };
    }
  }
  throw new Error('Claude returned no result.');
};
// The explorer's head start: what a quick deterministic scan already knows (ways in, routes, which requests hit which
// routes, which tables are written), so Claude spends its reading on the question instead of on finding the edges.
import * as fs from 'node:fs';
import { findFetchSites, initTreeSitter, matchRoute, scanRepoFacts, type RepoScan } from '@codemap/facts';

const MAX_LINES = 40;
const section = (title: string, lines: string[]) =>
  lines.length ? [`${title}:`, ...lines.slice(0, MAX_LINES), ...(lines.length > MAX_LINES ? [`  …and ${lines.length - MAX_LINES} more`] : []), ''] : [];

export async function headStart(root: string): Promise<{ text: string; scan: RepoScan | null }> {
  await initTreeSitter();
  let scan: RepoScan;
  try {
    scan = scanRepoFacts(root);
  } catch {
    return { text: '(The automatic scan could not read this repo; explore it directly.)', scan: null };
  }
  const facts = Object.values(scan.fileFacts);

  const entries = facts.flatMap((f) => f.entries).map((e) => `  - ${e.kind} ${e.label}${e.symbol ? ` → ${e.symbol}` : ` (${e.file})`}`);
  const routes = facts.flatMap((f) => f.routes);
  const routeLines = routes.map((r) => `  - ${r.method} ${r.path} → ${r.handler ?? r.file}`);

  const fetchFiles = facts
    .filter((f) => /\.(tsx?|jsx?|mjs|cjs)$/.test(f.path))
    .flatMap((f) => {
      const source = fs.readFileSync(`${root}/${f.path}`, 'utf8');
      return /\bfetch\(|axios|ky\./.test(source) ? [{ path: f.path, source, symbols: f.symbols }] : [];
    });
  const requests = findFetchSites(fetchFiles).flatMap((site) => {
    const m = matchRoute(site, routes);
    return m ? [`  - ${site.from} sends ${site.method} ${site.url} → ${m.route.handler ?? m.route.file}`] : [];
  });

  const writers = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  for (const f of facts) for (const w of f.writes) writers.set(w.table, (writers.get(w.table) ?? new Set()).add(w.symbol ?? f.path));
  const tables = [...writers].map(([t, by]) => `  - ${t} ← ${[...by].slice(0, 4).join(', ')}`);

  const folders = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const f of scan.files) {
    const top = f.includes('/') ? f.slice(0, f.indexOf('/')) : '(root)';
    folders.set(top, (folders.get(top) ?? 0) + 1);
  }
  const folderLines = [...folders].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).map(([d, n]) => `  - ${d}/ (${n} files)`);

  const text = [
    ...section('Ways in (entry points)', entries),
    ...section('Routes and their handlers', routeLines),
    ...section('Requests from the code that match a route', requests),
    ...section('Tables and what writes them', tables),
    ...section('Top-level folders', folderLines),
  ].join('\n');
  return { text: text || '(The automatic scan found no entry points; explore the repo directly.)', scan };
}
```

```text
function checkEdge(e: MapEdge, byId: ReadonlyMap<string, MapNode>, repo: RepoReader, facts: Facts, window: number): ClaimCheck {
  const evidence = e.evidence.map((x) => checkEvidence(repo, x, window));
  const reasons = evidenceReasons(evidence);
  const from = byId.get(e.from);
  const to = byId.get(e.to);
  if (reasons.length || !from || !to || e.kind === 'then') return result(evidence, reasons, 'text');

  if (e.kind === 'calls') {
    if (!from.symbol || !to.symbol) return result(evidence, reasons, 'text');
    const calls = facts.calls(fileOf(from.symbol), [fileOf(to.symbol)]);
    if (!calls.some((c) => within(c.from, from.symbol!) && c.to === to.symbol)) reasons.push(`the code has no call from ${from.symbol} to ${to.symbol}`);
    return result(evidence, reasons, 'fact');
  }

  const fromFile = from.symbol ? fileOf(from.symbol) : from.evidence[0]!.file;
  const toFile = to.symbol ? fileOf(to.symbol) : to.evidence[0]!.file;
  const fromFacts = facts.get(fromFile);
  if (!fromFacts) {
    reasons.push(`${fromFile} can't be read`);
    return result(evidence, reasons, 'fact');
  }

  if (e.kind === 'imports') {
    if (!fromFacts.imports.some((i) => i.to === toFile)) reasons.push(`${fromFile} doesn't import ${toFile}`);
    return result(evidence, reasons, 'fact');
  }

  // request: a fetch in the `from` box (direct, or through a wrapper it imports) that matches a route in the `to` box.
  const neighbours = [fromFile, ...fromFacts.imports.filter((i) => !i.to.startsWith('vendor:')).map((i) => i.to)];
  const sources = neighbours.flatMap((path) => {
    const source = repo.text(path);
    const f = facts.get(path);
    return source !== null && f ? [{ path, source, symbols: f.symbols }] : [];
  });
  const routes = facts.get(toFile)?.routes ?? [];
  const matched = findFetchSites(sources).some((site) => {
    if (site.file !== fromFile || (from.symbol && !within(site.from, from.symbol))) return false;
    const m = matchRoute(site, routes);
    return !!m && (to.symbol ? m.route.handler === to.symbol : true);
  });
  if (!matched) reasons.push(`no request from ${from.symbol ?? fromFile} matches a route handled by ${to.symbol ?? toFile}`);
  return result(evidence, reasons, 'fact');
}

function checkAbsence(a: MapAbsence, repo: RepoReader, files: readonly string[]): AbsenceCheck {
  let pattern: RegExp;
  try {
    pattern = new RegExp(a.search.regex ? a.search.pattern : a.search.pattern.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&'), 'g');
  } catch {
    return { status: 'unconfirmed', found: 0, locations: [], reasons: ['the search pattern is not a valid regular expression'] };
  }
  let found = 0;
  const locations: { file: string; line: number }[] = [];
  for (const file of files) {
    if (a.search.paths && !matchesAny(a.search.paths, file)) continue;
    const text = repo.text(file);
    if (text === null) continue;
    text.split('\n').forEach((line, i) => {
      const n = line.match(pattern)?.length ?? 0;
      if (!n) return;
      found += n;
      if (locations.length < MAX_LOCATIONS) locations.push({ file, line: i + 1 });
    });
  }
  const reasons = found === a.matches ? [] : [`the search finds ${found} ${found === 1 ? 'match' : 'matches'}; the map says ${a.matches}`];
  return { status: reasons.length ? 'unconfirmed' : 'confirmed', found, locations, reasons };
}
/** A repo-relative path that can't climb out of the repo: no absolute paths, no `..`, no backslashes. */
export function isSafeRelativePath(path: string): boolean {
  if (!path || path.startsWith('/') || path.includes('\\') || /^[A-Za-z]:/.test(path)) return false;
  return path.split('/').every((seg) => seg !== '..' && seg !== '');
}

/** Validates shape, then references: unique ids, edges between real boxes, tour stops that point at real things. */
export function parseMap(input: unknown): ParseResult {
  const parsed = CodeMap.safeParse(input);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    return { ok: false, problems: parsed.error.issues.map((i) => `${i.path.join('.') || '(map)'}: ${i.message}`) };
  }
  const map = parsed.data;
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const ids = (kind: string, items: readonly { id: string }[]) => {
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    for (const { id } of items) {
      if (seen.has(id)) problems.push(`${kind} id "${id}" is used twice`);
      seen.add(id);
    }
    return seen;
  };
  const areas = ids('area', map.areas);
  const nodes = ids('node', map.nodes);
  const edges = ids('edge', map.edges);
  const absences = ids('absence', map.absences);
  ids('tour stop', map.tour);

  const evidence = (where: string, list: readonly Evidence[]) => {
    for (const e of list) if (!isSafeRelativePath(e.file)) problems.push(`${where}: evidence file "${e.file}" must be a path inside the repo`);
  };
  for (const n of map.nodes) {
    if (!areas.has(n.area)) problems.push(`node "${n.id}": unknown area "${n.area}"`);
    if (n.symbol && !isSafeRelativePath(n.symbol.slice(0, n.symbol.indexOf('#')))) problems.push(`node "${n.id}": symbol file must be a path inside the repo`);
    evidence(`node "${n.id}"`, n.evidence);
  }
  for (const e of map.edges) {
    if (!nodes.has(e.from)) problems.push(`edge "${e.id}": unknown node "${e.from}"`);
    if (!nodes.has(e.to)) problems.push(`edge "${e.id}": unknown node "${e.to}"`);
    evidence(`edge "${e.id}"`, e.evidence);
  }
  for (const a of map.absences) {
    if (a.between && !nodes.has(a.between.from)) problems.push(`absence "${a.id}": unknown node "${a.between.from}"`);
    if (a.between && !nodes.has(a.between.to)) problems.push(`absence "${a.id}": unknown node "${a.between.to}"`);
  }
  for (const t of map.tour) {
    const refs: [string, readonly string[] | undefined, Set<string>][] = [
      ['area', t.focus.areas, areas], ['node', t.focus.nodes, nodes], ['edge', t.focus.edges, edges], ['absence', t.focus.absences, absences],
    ];
    for (const [kind, list, known] of refs) for (const id of list ?? []) if (!known.has(id)) problems.push(`tour stop "${t.id}": unknown ${kind} "${id}"`);
  }
  return problems.length ? { ok: false, problems } : { ok: true, map };
}
```

## The drafting loop

```
question → [scan] → [prompt] → CLAUDE → [shape check] → [claim check] → done? → [save] → [re-check] → browser
                                  ↑                                         │
                                  └────── [repair to-do list] ←── no ───────┘   (at most 2 repairs)
```

Everything in brackets is plain code. Claude is the one AI step.

| Step | What runs it | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Scan the repo (`hints.ts`) | **Code** | Finds entry points, routes, which requests hit which routes, and which tables get written. This becomes the "head start" section of the prompt. |
| Write the instructions (`prompts.ts`) | **Code** | Fills the question and the scan into a fixed set of instructions: what a good map is, how to cite code, how to write the walkthrough. |
| Explore and draft (`agent.ts`) | **Claude** | Reads the code with Read, Grep and Glob only (no edit, write or shell tools; secret files blocked). Returns JSON in a required shape. |
| Check the shape (`parseMap`) | **Code** | Correct fields, unique ids, arrows between boxes that exist, every path inside the repo. |
| Check every claim (`check()`) | **Code** | Re-reads each cited line, checks code facts, and re-runs each "nothing does X" search. |
| Repair request (`evidenceRepairPrompt`) | **Code** | Turns the failed claims into a to-do list and sends it back to Claude in the same session. |
| Pick, save, re-check, show | **Code** | Keeps the attempt with the fewest unconfirmed claims, saves it, checks it again, then sends it to the browser. |

Claude never sees the checker. It only gets the checker's verdict, as plain text, between rounds. That's one of the map's two red dashed "nothing does X" claims. The other: Claude is given no edit, write or shell tools.

## Where the AI part actually lives

All the judgment is Claude's: what counts as a step, what to name it, how to group things into areas, where the gaps are, and the walkthrough text. The checker doesn't grade any of that. Here is what "confirmed" actually guarantees, from reading `check.ts`:

- **Every box and arrow:** the quoted text really is on the cited line, allowing 3 lines of drift, or anywhere in the file if it appears exactly once.
- **Arrows marked `calls`, `imports` or `request`:** also verified against facts read from the code. The function really calls the other function, the file really imports the other file, or the request really matches the route.
- **Boxes with a function name attached:** that function really exists.
- **"Nothing does X":** the search really finds the number of matches the map claims, usually 0.
- **Walkthrough stops:** only checked for whether they point at confirmed boxes and arrows.

The gap is that arrows marked `then` only get the first check: the cited line exists. Whether the label is true isn't verified. In this map, 9 of the 11 arrows are `then`, including "if claims fail" and "same session, retry", so most of the 23 confirmations mean "the cited line exists", not "the arrow is true". Box names, explanations and walkthrough text aren't checked at all.

So "23 of 23 confirmed" means Claude couldn't make up citations or false function calls. It could still label a real line misleadingly. If you want the checker to do more, the next step would be to verify more kinds of arrow (events, retries, ordering) against code facts, so fewer of them rest on citations alone.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/johnzhang/.claude/skills/codemap

# codemap

codemap turns a question about this repo into a map the person can explore in their browser: areas of the app, the
steps in order, labeled arrows, and red dashed arrows where something that should be connected isn't. A plain program
checks every claim against the code before it's shown. In the map they can take a walkthrough, select any box or arrow
and ask about it, and approve fixes that codemap applies and re-checks.

## When to use it

- The user asks how something works across several files: "what happens when…", "how does X reach Y", "where does Z
  get triggered".
- The user is about to change code they don't understand yet and wants to see it first.
- The user asks for a map, diagram, graph or walkthrough of part of the code.

Don't use it for a question about a single line or function; answer that directly.

## How to run it

Run from the repo root (or pass `--repo`). Use the user's question in their own words:

```bash
codemap "What happens when a patient converts?" --repo "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
```

It starts a small local server, explores the code with Claude (about a minute for a small repo), and prints a link
like `http://127.0.0.1:4317/m/<id>?t=<token>`. Give the user that link and tell them to open it. The command keeps
running to serve the map: run it in the background, and don't wait for it to exit.

Other commands:

- `codemap open` lists the maps already made in this repo (they're saved under `.codemap/maps/`).
- `codemap check <map-id>` re-checks a saved map against the current code and prints anything that no longer holds.
  It exits with 1 if a claim fails, so it can run in CI.

## Notes

- codemap reads the code and never changes it, except for a fix the user approves in the map.
- It never reads secret files (`.env`, keys) and only listens on 127.0.0.1.
- It needs Claude access: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or a logged-in Claude Code.
- If `codemap` isn't on the PATH, it hasn't been installed. Tell the user to install it from the codemap repo
  (see its README) instead of guessing another command.

```text
// Changing a map after it's made: what the explainer finds is added, a fix's new connection is drawn, a missing
// connection that a fix closed is dropped. Every change goes back through `parseMap`, so ids stay unique and references
// stay valid.
import { parseMap, type CodeMap, type ParseResult } from './format';

/** New areas, boxes, arrows and missing connections, as the model wrote them (validated on merge). */
export type MapAdditions = { areas?: unknown[]; nodes?: unknown[]; edges?: unknown[]; absences?: unknown[] };

export function addToMap(map: CodeMap, add: MapAdditions): ParseResult {
  return parseMap({
    ...map,
    areas: [...map.areas, ...(add.areas ?? [])],
    nodes: [...map.nodes, ...(add.nodes ?? [])],
    edges: [...map.edges, ...(add.edges ?? [])],
    absences: [...map.absences, ...(add.absences ?? [])],
  });
}

export function removeAbsences(map: CodeMap, ids: readonly string[]): CodeMap {
  const drop = new Set(ids);
  return {
    ...map,
    absences: map.absences.filter((a) => !drop.has(a.id)),
    tour: map.tour.map((t) => (t.focus.absences ? { ...t, focus: { ...t.focus, absences: t.focus.absences.filter((id) => !drop.has(id)) } } : t)),
  };
}

/** Ids of everything in the map, for picking new ones. */
export function mapIds(map: CodeMap): Set<string> {
  return new Set([...map.areas, ...map.nodes, ...map.edges, ...map.absences, ...map.tour].map((x) => x.id));
}

export function freshId(map: CodeMap, prefix: string): string {
  const taken = mapIds(map);
  for (let i = 1; ; i++) if (!taken.has(`${prefix}${i}`)) return `${prefix}${i}`;
}

/** A short, file-safe id for a map from its question. */
export function slugify(question: string): string {
  const slug = question
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/['’]/g, '')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')
    .split('-')
    .filter((w) => !['what', 'happens', 'when', 'the', 'a', 'an', 'does', 'do', 'how', 'is', 'are', 'it', 'go', 'out'].includes(w))
    .slice(0, 6)
    .join('-');
  return slug || 'map';
}
```

Short answer: nothing gets remapped. After the first map, follow-up questions only add to it. Nothing already on the map is redrawn or replaced, and anything new has to pass the checker first.

## A follow-up question in the viewer

1. **You ask.** Optionally select boxes, arrows or gaps first, then type a question. The browser sends it to the server.
2. **One job at a time per map.** If Claude is still working on that map, the server refuses the question with "try again when it finishes".
3. **Claude answers** (`explainer.ts`). It gets the whole current map, a list of which claims the checker couldn't confirm, your selection and your question. It can read more of the code. It returns:
   - an answer at three depths: concept, how it works, code
   - which parts of the map the answer relies on
   - which boxes to highlight
   - any new boxes, arrows or gaps to add
   - a fix, if you asked for a change
4. **New parts are merged, then checked** (`addToMap`). The additions go through the same shape check as a new map, then `check()`. Any addition that fails is removed before anyone sees it, with a note in the answer: "Not drawn, couldn't confirm…".

   This is stricter than making the first map: there are no repair rounds, and nothing new is shown with a "?". New parts either pass or don't appear.
5. **Saved and redrawn.** If anything new survived, the bigger map is saved and every open tab redraws, with "NEW" badges on the added parts. Otherwise the map stays the same and only the answer appears.

## Asking about a separate component
- **On the same map:** the question grows that map. Claude explores the new part and adds an area with its boxes, connected to the existing ones where the code really connects them. Asking a question on a map never starts a separate map; that's one of the map's two "nothing does X" claims.
- **As its own map:** start a new question from the home page, or run `codemap "<question>"` again. That's a fresh draft-and-check loop and a separate map file, with no link to the first map.

## Things the map got slightly wrong or left out
- **The Claude session.** The map says each answer continues the same Claude session, so Claude remembers what it already read. That's only true from the second follow-up on. The first follow-up starts a new session, separate from the one that drew the map, with the map handed over as JSON. So Claude doesn't remember the files it read while drawing the map, and may read them again.
- **The walkthrough doesn't grow.** New boxes don't get walkthrough stops; the walkthrough only covers what the first map had.
- **Answers are lost on restart.** Answers and proposed fixes live in server memory, while the added boxes are saved in the map file. After a restart you keep the bigger map but lose the conversation that explains why it grew. The map lists this as its second "nothing does X" claim.
- **The prompt gets bigger.** Every question resends the whole map, so long sessions on a busy map send more each time.

```text
// The codemap command.
//   codemap "<question>"        map a question about the repo, then open the map
//   codemap open [<map-id>]     open saved maps
//   codemap check <map-id|file> re-check a saved map against the code (exit 1 if anything is unconfirmed)
//   codemap list                list saved maps
// Options: --repo <dir> (default: current directory)  --port <n> (default 4317)  --no-open  --model <id>
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import * as fs from 'node:fs';
import * as path from 'node:path';
import { check, initTreeSitterForChecks, parseMap } from './cli-support';
import { startServer } from './server';
import { createStore } from './store';

type Args = { command: 'map' | 'open' | 'check' | 'list' | 'help'; rest: string[]; repo: string; port: number; open: boolean; model?: string };

function parseArgs(argv: string[]): Args {
  const flags: Record<string, string | boolean> = {};
  const positional: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
    const a = argv[i]!;
    if (a === '--no-open') flags.open = false;
    else if (a === '-h' || a === '--help') flags.help = true;
    else if (a.startsWith('--')) flags[a.slice(2)] = argv[++i] ?? '';
    else positional.push(a);
  }
  const first = positional[0];
  const command = flags.help || !first ? 'help' : (['open', 'check', 'list', 'help'].includes(first) ? first : 'map') as Args['command'];
  return {
    command,
    rest: command === 'map' ? [positional.join(' ')] : positional.slice(1),
    repo: path.resolve(String(flags.repo ?? process.cwd())),
    port: Number(flags.port ?? 4317),
    open: flags.open !== false,
    model: typeof flags.model === 'string' ? flags.model : undefined,
  };
}

function openBrowser(url: string) {
  const [cmd, args] = process.platform === 'darwin' ? ['open', [url]] : process.platform === 'win32' ? ['cmd', ['/c', 'start', '', url]] : ['xdg-open', [url]];
  spawn(cmd as string, args as string[], { stdio: 'ignore', detached: true }).unref();
}

const HELP = `codemap: ask how your code works, get a map you can point at.

  codemap "<question>"          map a question about this repo and open it
  codemap open [<map-id>]       open saved maps
  codemap check <map-id|file>   re-check a saved map against the code
  codemap list                  list saved maps

Options: --repo <dir>  --port <n>  --no-open  --model <id>
Needs Claude: an Anthropic API key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) or a logged-in Claude Code.`;

async function main() {
  const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
  if (args.command === 'help') return console.log(HELP);
  if (!fs.existsSync(args.repo)) throw new Error(`No such folder: ${args.repo}`);

  if (args.command === 'list') {
    const maps = createStore(args.repo).list();
    if (!maps.length) return console.log('No maps yet. Try: codemap "what happens when …?"');
    for (const m of maps) console.log(`${m.id}  ${m.question}`);
    return;
  }

  if (args.command === 'check') {
    const target = args.rest[0];
    if (!target) throw new Error('Which map? codemap check <map-id|file>');
    await initTreeSitterForChecks();
    const raw = fs.existsSync(target) ? (JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(target, 'utf8')) as { map?: unknown }) : createStore(args.repo).get(target);
    if (!raw) throw new Error(`No map "${target}" in ${args.repo}/.codemap/maps`);
    const parsed = parseMap('map' in raw ? raw.map : raw);
    if (!parsed.ok) throw new Error(`The map isn't valid:\n${parsed.problems.join('\n')}`);
    const report = check(parsed.map, args.repo);
    console.log(`${report.summary.confirmed} of ${report.summary.claims} claims confirmed`);
    for (const [kind, group] of [['box', report.nodes], ['arrow', report.edges], ['missing connection', report.absences]] as const) {
      for (const [id, c] of Object.entries(group)) if (c.status !== 'confirmed') console.log(`  ✗ ${kind} ${id}: ${c.reasons.join('; ')}`);
    }
    process.exitCode = report.summary.unconfirmed ? 1 : 0;
    return;
  }

  const server = await startServer({ root: args.repo, port: args.port, model: args.model });
  let url: string;
  if (args.command === 'map') {
    const id = server.startMap(args.rest[0] ?? '');
    url = server.pageUrl(id);
    console.log(`Mapping "${args.rest[0]}" in ${args.repo}`);
  } else {
    url = server.pageUrl(args.rest[0]);
  }
  console.log(`\n  ${url}\n\nOpen that link to see the map. Press Ctrl+C to stop.`);
  if (args.open) openBrowser(url);
  const stop = () => void server.close().then(() => process.exit(0));
  process.on('SIGINT', stop);
  process.on('SIGTERM', stop);
}

main().catch((err: unknown) => {
  console.error(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));
  process.exit(1);
```
