      return json(res, 200, { ...stored, report: check(stored.map, root), job, failure: null, answers: answers.get(mapId) ?? [], fixes: fixStates(mapId) });
    }
    if (mapId && parts[2] === 'ask' && m === 'POST') {
      const body = await readBody(req);
      startAsk(mapId, String(body.question ?? ''), asSelection(body.selection));
      return json(res, 202, { ok: true });
    }
    if (mapId && parts[2] === 'recheck' && m === 'POST') {
      const stored = store.get(mapId);
      if (!stored) throw new HttpError(404, 'No such map.');
      return json(res, 200, { report: publishMap(stored) });
    }
    if (mapId && parts[2] === 'fixes' && parts[3] && m === 'POST') {
      const fixId = parts[3];
      if (parts[4] === 'approve') return json(res, 200, approveFix(mapId, fixId));
      if (parts[4] === 'undo') { undo(mapId, fixId); return json(res, 200, { ok: true }); }
      if (parts[4] === 'reject') {
        if (proposals.get(fixId)?.mapId !== mapId) throw new HttpError(404, 'No such fix waiting for approval.');
        proposals.delete(fixId);
        broadcast({ type: 'fix', mapId, fixId, status: 'rejected' });
        return json(res, 200, { ok: true });
      }
    }
    throw new HttpError(404, 'Not found.');
  }

  function serveStatic(res: http.ServerResponse, pathname: string) {
    const index = path.join(viewerDir, 'index.html');
    if (!fs.existsSync(index)) {
      res.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' });
      return res.end('<!doctype html><meta charset="utf-8"><title>codemap</title><p style="font:16px system-ui;margin:40px">The viewer isn\'t built yet. Run <code>npm run build</code> in the codemap repo, then reload.</p>');
    }
    const rel = decodeURIComponent(pathname).replace(/^\/+/, '');
    const file = path.resolve(viewerDir, rel);
    const inside = file.startsWith(path.resolve(viewerDir) + path.sep);
    const target = inside && rel.startsWith('assets/') && fs.existsSync(file) && fs.statSync(file).isFile() ? file : index;
    res.writeHead(200, {
      'content-type': TYPES[path.extname(target)] ?? 'application/octet-stream',
      'cache-control': target === index ? 'no-store' : 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable',
      'x-content-type-options': 'nosniff',
      ...(target === index ? { 'content-security-policy': "default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ws://127.0.0.1:* ws://localhost:*; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self'" } : {}),
    });
    fs.createReadStream(target).pipe(res);
  }

  const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
    void (async () => {
      try {
        const url = new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://localhost');
        if (!hostOk(req)) throw new HttpError(403, 'Wrong host.');
        if (url.pathname.startsWith('/api/')) {
          if (!tokenOk(req.headers['x-codemap-token'])) throw new HttpError(401, 'Missing or wrong token. Open codemap from the link it printed.');
          if (req.method !== 'GET' && !originOk(req)) throw new HttpError(403, 'Wrong origin.');
          return await api(req, res, url);
        }
        if (req.method !== 'GET') throw new HttpError(405, 'Method not allowed.');
        return serveStatic(res, url.pathname);
      } catch (err) {
        if (err instanceof HttpError) return json(res, err.status, { error: err.message, ...err.extra });
        return json(res, 500, { error: errorText(err) });
      }
    })();
  });

  const wss = new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true });
  server.on('upgrade', (req, socket, head) => {
    const url = new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://localhost');
    if (url.pathname !== '/ws' || !hostOk(req) || !originOk(req) || !tokenOk(url.searchParams.get('t'))) {
      socket.write('HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\n\r\n');
      socket.destroy();
      return;
    }
    wss.handleUpgrade(req, socket, head, (ws) => {
      clients.add(ws);
      ws.on('close', () => clients.delete(ws));
    });
  });

  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    const onError = (err: NodeJS.ErrnoException) => {
      if (err.code === 'EADDRINUSE' && o.port) {
        server.off('error', onError);
        server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => resolve());
      } else reject(err);
    };
    server.on('error', onError);
    server.listen(o.port ?? 0, '127.0.0.1', () => resolve());
  });
  port = (server.address() as { port: number }).port;
  const url = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;

  return {
    url,
    port,
    token,
    pageUrl: (mapId?: string) => `${url}/${mapId ? `m/${mapId}` : ''}?t=${token}`,
    startMap,
    close: () =>
      new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
        for (const ws of clients) ws.terminate();
        wss.close();
        server.close(() => resolve());
      }),
  };
}

// Talking to the local codemap server. The token comes from the link codemap printed (`?t=…`) and goes on every call.
import type { Answer, CheckReport, CodeMap, MapMeta, Selection, ServerEvent } from './types';

function readToken(): string {
  const fromUrl = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('t');
  try {
    if (fromUrl) sessionStorage.setItem('codemap-token', fromUrl);
    return fromUrl ?? sessionStorage.getItem('codemap-token') ?? '';
  } catch {
    return fromUrl ?? '';
  }
}

export const token = readToken();
export const pageUrl = (mapId?: string) => `/${mapId ? `m/${encodeURIComponent(mapId)}` : ''}?t=${encodeURIComponent(token)}`;

export class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string, readonly problems: string[] = []) {
    super(message);
  }
}

async function call<T>(method: string, path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T> {
  const res = await fetch(path, {
    method,
    headers: { 'x-codemap-token': token, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  const data = (await res.json().catch(() => ({}))) as { error?: string; problems?: string[] };
  if (!res.ok) throw new ApiError(data.error ?? `Request failed (${res.status})`, data.problems ?? []);
  return data as T;
}

export type JobInfo = { kind: 'make' | 'ask'; question: string; progress: string[] };
export type MapPayload = {
  meta: MapMeta | null;
  map: CodeMap | null;
  report: CheckReport | null;
  job: JobInfo | null;
  failure: { question: string; error: string } | null;
  answers: Answer[];
  /** Fixes that are waiting for approval or applied; any other fix was rejected. */
  fixes?: Record<string, { status: 'proposed' | 'applied'; edgeId?: string | null; closed?: string[] }>;
};

export const api = {
  list: () => call<{ repo: string; maps: MapMeta[]; making: { id: string; question: string }[] }>('GET', '/api/maps'),
  get: (id: string) => call<MapPayload>('GET', `/api/maps/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`),
  make: (question: string) => call<{ id: string }>('POST', '/api/maps', { question }),
  ask: (id: string, question: string, selection: Selection) => call<{ ok: true }>('POST', `/api/maps/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/ask`, { question, selection }),
  approve: (id: string, fixId: string) =>
    call<{ edgeId: string | null; closed: string[]; files: string[] }>('POST', `/api/maps/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/fixes/${encodeURIComponent(fixId)}/approve`),
  reject: (id: string, fixId: string) => call<{ ok: true }>('POST', `/api/maps/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/fixes/${encodeURIComponent(fixId)}/reject`),
  undo: (id: string, fixId: string) => call<{ ok: true }>('POST', `/api/maps/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/fixes/${encodeURIComponent(fixId)}/undo`),
};

/** Live events from the server. Reconnects after a drop; returns a function that stops listening. */
export function connect(onEvent: (e: ServerEvent) => void, onStatus: (connected: boolean) => void): () => void {
  let ws: WebSocket | null = null;
  let stopped = false;
  let retry: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  const open = () => {
    ws = new WebSocket(`${location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss' : 'ws'}://${location.host}/ws?t=${encodeURIComponent(token)}`);
    ws.onopen = () => onStatus(true);
    ws.onmessage = (m) => {
      try {
        onEvent(JSON.parse(String(m.data)) as ServerEvent);
      } catch {
        /* ignore malformed frames */
      }
    };
    ws.onclose = () => {
      onStatus(false);
      if (!stopped) retry = setTimeout(open, 1000);
    };
  };
  open();
  return () => {
    stopped = true;
    if (retry) clearTimeout(retry);
    ws?.close();
  };
}
// The two screens: the list of maps (with a box to ask a new question), and a map with its panel and input bar.
import { useCallback, useEffect, useReducer, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { ReactFlowProvider } from '@xyflow/react';
import { ApiError, api, connect, pageUrl, token } from './api';
import { Composer } from './composer';

import { Home } from './home';
import { Panel } from './panel';
import { currentView, initialState, reducer, type Sel } from './state';
import type { CheckReport, CodeMap } from './types';

export function App() {
  if (!token) {
    return (
      <main className="home">
        <h1>Open codemap from its link</h1>
        <p className="muted lede">This page needs the link codemap printed in your terminal (it ends in <code>?t=…</code>). That keeps other websites from talking to your local codemap.</p>
      </main>
    );
  }
  const m = /^\/m\/([a-z0-9-]{1,80})\/?$/.exec(location.pathname);
  return m ? <MapScreen mapId={m[1]!} /> : <Home />;
}

function Summary({ report }: { report: CheckReport | null }) {
  if (!report) return null;
  const { claims, confirmed, unconfirmed } = report.summary;
  return unconfirmed
    ? <span className="summary warn" title="Some claims didn't check out against the code; they're marked with ?">✓ {confirmed} of {claims} confirmed · {unconfirmed} couldn't be</span>
    : <span className="summary ok" title="Every box and arrow was checked against the code">✓ All {claims} claims confirmed</span>;
}

function JumpTo({ map, onPick }: { map: CodeMap; onPick: (id: string) => void }) {
  const [text, setText] = useState('');
  return (
    <form
      className="jump"
      onSubmit={(e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        const q = text.trim().toLowerCase();
        const hit = map.nodes.find((n) => n.name.toLowerCase() === q) ?? map.nodes.find((n) => n.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || n.symbol?.toLowerCase().includes(q));
        if (hit) { onPick(hit.id); setText(''); }
      }}
    >
      <input id="jump" list="jump-names" value={text} onChange={(e) => setText(e.target.value)} placeholder="⌕ Jump to…" aria-label="Jump to a step" />
      <datalist id="jump-names">{map.nodes.map((n) => <option key={n.id} value={n.name} />)}</datalist>
    </form>
  );
}

function MapScreen({ mapId }: { mapId: string }) {
  const [s, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, mapId, initialState);
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState('');
  const [pick, setPick] = useState(false);
  const wasConnected = useRef(false);

  const load = useCallback(() => {
    api.get(mapId).then(
      (payload) => dispatch({ type: 'loaded', payload }),
      (e: Error) => dispatch(e instanceof ApiError && /No such map/.test(e.message) ? { type: 'missing' } : { type: 'error', message: e.message }),
    );
  }, [mapId]);

  useEffect(load, [load]);
  useEffect(
    () =>
      connect(
        (event) => dispatch({ type: 'event', event }),
        (value) => {
          dispatch({ type: 'connected', value });
          if (value && wasConnected.current === false && s.phase !== 'loading') load(); // catch up after a reconnect
          wasConnected.current = value;
        },
      ),
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
    [],
  );

  const ask = useCallback(
    (question: string) => {
      const q = question.trim();
      if (!q || s.job) return;
      api.ask(mapId, q, s.selection).then(() => setDraft(''), (e: Error) => dispatch({ type: 'error', message: e.message }));
    },
    [mapId, s.job, s.selection],
  );

  const onFix = (fixId: string, action: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'undo') => {
    if (action === 'approve') dispatch({ type: 'fixStatus', fixId, status: 'applying', problems: [] });
    api[action](mapId, fixId).catch((e: ApiError) => {
      if (action === 'approve') dispatch({ type: 'fixStatus', fixId, status: 'failed', problems: e.problems.length ? e.problems : [e.message] });
      else dispatch({ type: 'error', message: [e.message, ...e.problems].join(' ') });
    });
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      const typing = e.target instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement || e.target instanceof HTMLInputElement;
      if (e.key === 'Escape') {
        if (s.tour !== null) dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: null });
        else dispatch({ type: 'clearSelection' });
        return;
      }
      if (typing || s.tour === null) return;
      if (e.key === 'ArrowRight') dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: s.tour + 1 });
      if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft') dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: s.tour - 1 });
    };
    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey);
  }, [s.tour]);

  const shown = s.answers.find((a) => a.id === s.shown);
  const pendingFix = shown?.fix && ['proposed', 'applying', 'failed'].includes(s.fixes[shown.fix.id]?.status ?? '') ? shown.fix : null;
  const onSelect = useCallback((kind: keyof Sel, id: string, additive: boolean) => dispatch({ type: 'select', kind, id, additive }), []);
  const onSelectMany = useCallback((selection: Sel) => dispatch({ type: 'selectMany', selection }), []);
  const onClear = useCallback(() => dispatch({ type: 'clearSelection' }), []);

  return (
    <div className="app">
      <header className="topbar">
        <a className="brand" href={pageUrl()}>codemap</a>
        <span className="nav">
          <button aria-label="Back" disabled={s.viewIndex < 0} onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'back' })}>◀</button>
          <button aria-label="Forward" disabled={s.viewIndex >= s.views.length - 1} onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'forward' })}>▶</button>
        </span>
        <span className="topq">{s.map?.question ?? s.job?.question ?? ''}</span>
        <Summary report={s.report} />
        <span className="grow" />
        {s.map && <JumpTo map={s.map} onPick={(id) => dispatch({ type: 'focus', id })} />}
        {s.map && <button className={pick ? 'tool on' : 'tool'} aria-pressed={pick} onClick={() => setPick(!pick)} title="Drag around a region to select it">⬚ Pick</button>}
        {s.map && s.map.tour.length > 0 && <button className="tool" onClick={() => dispatch({ type: 'tour', stop: s.tour === null ? 0 : null })}>{s.tour === null ? 'Walkthrough' : 'Leave walkthrough'}</button>}
        <span className={s.connected ? 'live on' : 'live'} title={s.connected ? 'Connected to codemap' : 'Reconnecting to codemap…'} />
      </header>
      <div className="body">
        <div className="canvas">
          {s.map ? (
            <>
              <ReactFlowProvider>
                <MapGraph map={s.map} report={s.report} selection={s.selection} view={currentView(s)} fresh={s.fresh} ghost={pendingFix ?? null} pick={pick} onSelect={onSelect} onSelectMany={onSelectMany} onClear={onClear} />
              </ReactFlowProvider>
              <Composer
                map={s.map}
                selection={s.selection}
                draft={draft}
                busy={!!s.job}
                onDraft={setDraft}
                onRemove={(kind, id) => dispatch({ type: 'select', kind, id, additive: true })}
                onSend={() => ask(draft)}
              />
            </>
          ) : (
            <div className="empty">{s.phase === 'making' ? <div className="pulse">Claude is exploring the code…</div> : null}</div>
          )}
        </div>
        <Panel state={s} dispatch={dispatch} onAsk={ask} onDraft={setDraft} onFix={onFix} onFocus={(id) => dispatch({ type: 'focus', id })} />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
// The start page: maps already made in this repo, and a box to ask a new question.
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { api, pageUrl } from './api';
import type { MapMeta } from './types';

export function Home() {
  const [repo, setRepo] = useState('');
  const [maps, setMaps] = useState<MapMeta[] | null>(null);
  const [making, setMaking] = useState<{ id: string; question: string }[]>([]);
  const [question, setQuestion] = useState('');
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    api.list().then((r) => { setRepo(r.repo); setMaps(r.maps); setMaking(r.making); }, (e: Error) => setError(e.message));
  }, []);

  const submit = async () => {
    if (!question.trim()) return;
    setBusy(true);
    try {
      const { id } = await api.make(question.trim());
      location.assign(pageUrl(id));
    } catch (e) {
      setError((e as Error).message);
      setBusy(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <main className="home">
      <div className="eyebrow">codemap{repo ? ` · ${repo}` : ''}</div>
      <h1>Ask how your code works</h1>
      <p className="muted lede">Claude explores the repo and draws the answer as a map. Every box and arrow is checked against the code before you see it.</p>
      <form className="home-ask" onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); void submit(); }}>
        <input id="question" value={question} onChange={(e) => setQuestion(e.target.value)} placeholder="What happens when a user signs up?" aria-label="Your question" autoFocus />
        <button className="btn primary" disabled={busy || !question.trim()}>{busy ? 'Starting…' : 'Map it'}</button>
      </form>
      {error && <div className="banner banner-dead" role="alert">{error}</div>}
      {making.length > 0 && (
        <section>
          <h2 className="section-title">Being made now</h2>
          <ul className="maplist">{making.map((m) => <li key={m.id}><a href={pageUrl(m.id)}>{m.question}</a><span className="muted small">Claude is exploring…</span></li>)}</ul>
        </section>
      )}
      <section>
        <h2 className="section-title">Maps in this repo</h2>
        {maps === null ? <p className="muted">Loading…</p> : maps.length === 0 ? <p className="muted">None yet. Ask a question above.</p> : (
          <ul className="maplist">
            {maps.map((m) => (
              <li key={m.id}>
                <a href={pageUrl(m.id)}>{m.question}</a>
                <span className="muted small">{new Date(m.updatedAt).toLocaleString()}{m.commit ? ` · ${m.commit.slice(0, 7)}` : ''}</span>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        )}
      </section>
    </main>
  );
}
import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import '@xyflow/react/dist/style.css';
import './styles.css';
import { App } from './app';

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(

    <App />

// Everything the map screen shows, as a pure reducer over server payloads, live events and clicks.
import type { MapPayload } from './api';
import type { Answer, CheckReport, CodeMap, FixProposal, MapMeta, Selection, ServerEvent } from './types';

export type Sel = { nodes: string[]; edges: string[]; absences: string[] };
export const emptySel = (): Sel => ({ nodes: [], edges: [], absences: [] });
export const selSize = (s: Sel) => s.nodes.length + s.edges.length + s.absences.length;

/** Where the map is looking: one item in focus, and what's lit up (everything else dims). */
export type View = { focus: string | null; highlight: string[] };
export type Depth = 'concept' | 'how' | 'code';
export type FixState = {
  proposal: FixProposal;
  answerId: string;
  status: 'proposed' | 'applying' | 'applied' | 'rejected' | 'undone' | 'failed';
  problems: string[];
  edgeId: string | null;
  closed: string[];
};

export type State = {
  mapId: string;
  phase: 'loading' | 'making' | 'ready' | 'failed' | 'missing';
  meta: MapMeta | null;
  map: CodeMap | null;
  report: CheckReport | null;
  job: { kind: 'make' | 'ask'; question: string; progress: string[] } | null;
  error: string | null;
  answers: Answer[];
  /** The answer shown in the panel. */
  shown: string | null;
  selection: Sel;
  /** Walkthrough stop, while touring. */
  tour: number | null;
  views: View[];
  viewIndex: number;
  depth: Depth;
  fixes: Record<string, FixState>;
  /** Added to the map by the latest answer (drawn with a NEW badge). */
  fresh: string[];
  connected: boolean;
};

export type Action =
  | { type: 'loaded'; payload: MapPayload }
  | { type: 'missing' }
  | { type: 'event'; event: ServerEvent }
  | { type: 'connected'; value: boolean }
  | { type: 'select'; kind: keyof Sel; id: string; additive: boolean }
  | { type: 'selectMany'; selection: Sel }
  | { type: 'clearSelection' }
  | { type: 'tour'; stop: number | null }
  | { type: 'focus'; id: string }
  | { type: 'back' }
  | { type: 'forward' }
  | { type: 'depth'; depth: Depth }
  | { type: 'show'; answerId: string | null }
  | { type: 'fixStatus'; fixId: string; status: FixState['status']; problems?: string[] }
  | { type: 'error'; message: string | null };

export const initialState = (mapId: string): State => ({
  mapId,
  phase: 'loading',
  meta: null,
  map: null,
  report: null,
  job: null,
  error: null,
  answers: [],
  shown: null,
  selection: emptySel(),
  tour: null,
  views: [],
  viewIndex: -1,
  depth: 'concept',
  fixes: {},
  fresh: [],
  connected: false,
});

export const currentView = (s: State): View | null => s.views[s.viewIndex] ?? null;

/** What a tour stop lights up: its boxes, arrows and gaps, and every box in the areas it names. */
export function stopView(map: CodeMap, stop: number): View | null {
  const t = map.tour[stop];
  if (!t) return null;
  const inAreas = map.nodes.filter((n) => t.focus.areas?.includes(n.area)).map((n) => n.id);
  const highlight = [...(t.focus.nodes ?? []), ...(t.focus.edges ?? []), ...(t.focus.absences ?? []), ...inAreas];
  const between = (t.focus.edges ?? []).length || (t.focus.absences ?? []).length ? [] : edgesWithin(map, new Set(highlight));
  return { focus: t.focus.nodes?.[0] ?? t.focus.edges?.[0] ?? t.focus.absences?.[0] ?? null, highlight: [...new Set([...highlight, ...between])] };
}

/** Arrows whose both ends are in `ids` (so a highlighted path shows its arrows too). */
export function edgesWithin(map: CodeMap, ids: ReadonlySet<string>): string[] {
  return map.edges.filter((e) => ids.has(e.from) && ids.has(e.to)).map((e) => e.id);
}

function pushView(s: State, view: View | null): State {
  if (!view) return s;
  const views = [...s.views.slice(0, s.viewIndex + 1), view].slice(-50);

// The local server end to end over HTTP and WebSocket, with a scripted Claude: make a map, ask, approve a fix, undo.
import * as http from 'node:http';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import WebSocket from 'ws';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { CARE_MAP, LISTENER_FIX, cleanup, copyCareApp, scriptedAgent, waitFor } from './helpers';

let server: CodemapServer;
let root: string;
const events: ServerEvent[] = [];
let ws: WebSocket;

const agent = scriptedAgent([
  () => CARE_MAP,
  () => ({ concept: 'Nothing listens for the announcement, so the rules never run from here.', refs: ['miss'], moves: { focus: 's4', highlight: ['s4', 'miss'] }, followUps: [] }),
  () => ({ concept: 'Add a listener.', refs: ['miss'], fix: LISTENER_FIX }),
]);

const api = async (method: string, path: string, body?: unknown, headers: Record<string, string> = {}) => {
  const res = await fetch(`${server.url}${path}`, {
    method,
    headers: { 'x-codemap-token': server.token, 'content-type': 'application/json', ...headers },
    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  return { status: res.status, body: (await res.json()) as any };
};

beforeAll(async () => {
  root = copyCareApp();
  server = await startServer({ root, port: 0, agent, viewerDir: join(root, 'no-viewer') });
  ws = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${server.port}/ws?t=${server.token}`);
  ws.on('message', (d) => events.push(JSON.parse(String(d))));
  await new Promise((r) => ws.once('open', r));
});
afterAll(async () => {
  ws.close();
  await server.close();
  cleanup();
});

  });

    const a = await waitFor(() => events.find((e) => e.type === 'answer'));

    expect(existsSync(join(root, 'src/automations/listeners.ts'))).toBe(true);
    const after = await api('GET', `/api/maps/${mapId}`);

    expect(after.body.map.absences).toEqual([]);
    expect(after.body.fixes).toEqual({ [fixId]: { status: 'applied', edgeId: 'fx1', closed: ['miss'] } }); // a reload can still offer Undo

// Stopping codemap from the page, and what a tab shows once it has stopped (by the button, Ctrl+C, or on its own).
import { api } from './api';

export function StopButton({ busy, onStopped, onError }: { busy: boolean; onStopped: () => void; onError: (message: string) => void }) {
  return (
    <button
      className="tool"
      disabled={busy}
      title={busy ? 'Claude is still working. You can stop codemap once it finishes.' : 'Stop codemap on this computer. Maps stay saved in the repo; answers and Undo don\'t carry over.'}
      onClick={() => api.stop().then(onStopped, (e: Error) => onError(e.message))}
    >
      Stop codemap
    </button>
  );
}

export function Stopped() {
  return (
    <main className="home">
      <h1>codemap has stopped</h1>
      <p className="muted lede">
        Your maps are saved in the repo under <code>.codemap/maps</code>. To see them again, run <code>codemap open</code> in
        the repo. You can close this tab.
      </p>
    </main>
  );
}

// The server stops itself when nobody is looking (no tab open, Claude not working) and from the page's Stop button.
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import WebSocket from 'ws';
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type { Agent } from '../src/agent';
import { STOPPED_CLOSE_CODE, startServer, type CodemapServer, type ServerOptions } from '../src/server';
import { CARE_MAP, cleanup, copyCareApp, waitFor } from './helpers';

const servers: CodemapServer[] = [];
afterEach(async () => {
  await Promise.all(servers.splice(0).map((s) => s.close()));
  cleanup();
});

/** A Claude stand-in that returns the care-app map only when `release()` is called. */
function heldAgent() {
  let release = () => {};
  const held = new Promise<void>((r) => (release = r));
  const agent: Agent = async () => {
    await held;
    return { output: CARE_MAP, sessionId: 'held', cost: 0 };
  };
  return { agent, release: () => release() };
}

async function start(o: Partial<ServerOptions> = {}) {
  const root = copyCareApp();
  const stops: string[] = [];
  const server = await startServer({ root, port: 0, viewerDir: join(root, 'no-viewer'), onStop: (r) => stops.push(r), ...o });
  servers.push(server);
  return { server, root, stops };
}

function tab(server: CodemapServer) {
  const ws = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${server.port}/ws?t=${server.token}`);
  const closed = new Promise<number>((r) => ws.once('close', (code) => r(code)));
  return { ws, closed, open: new Promise((r) => ws.once('open', r)) };
}

const stopRequest = (server: CodemapServer) =>
  fetch(`${server.url}/api/stop`, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'x-codemap-token': server.token } });
const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

describe('stopping codemap', () => {
  it('stays up while a tab is open, and stops a little after the last one closes', async () => {
    const { server, stops } = await start({ autoStop: { afterLastTabMs: 50, beforeFirstTabMs: 10_000 } });
    const t = tab(server);
    await t.open;
    await sleep(150);
    expect(stops).toEqual([]);
    t.ws.close();
    await waitFor(() => stops.length > 0);
    expect(stops).toEqual(['idle']);
    await expect(fetch(server.url)).rejects.toThrow();
  });

  it('keeps going while a reloaded tab reconnects within the grace period', async () => {
    const { server, stops } = await start({ autoStop: { afterLastTabMs: 150, beforeFirstTabMs: 10_000 } });
    const first = tab(server);
    await first.open;
    first.ws.close();
    await first.closed;
    const second = tab(server);
    await second.open;
    await sleep(300);
    expect(stops).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('never stops while Claude is working, even with no tab open', async () => {
    const { agent, release } = heldAgent();
    const { server, root, stops } = await start({ agent, autoStop: { afterLastTabMs: 20, beforeFirstTabMs: 20 } });
    const id = server.startMap('What happens when a patient converts?');
    await sleep(150);
    expect(stops).toEqual([]);
    release();
    await waitFor(() => stops.length > 0);
    expect(stops).toEqual(['idle']);
    expect(existsSync(join(root, `.codemap/maps/${id}.json`))).toBe(true); // the map was saved before stopping
  });

  it('does nothing on its own without autoStop', async () => {
    const { server, stops } = await start();
    const t = tab(server);
    await t.open;
    t.ws.close();
    await sleep(100);
    expect(stops).toEqual([]);
    expect((await fetch(server.url)).status).toBe(200);
  });

  it('stops from the page, refusing while Claude works, and tells open tabs it stopped', async () => {
    const { agent, release } = heldAgent();
    const { server, stops } = await start({ agent });
    server.startMap('What happens when a patient converts?');
    const busy = await stopRequest(server);
    expect(busy.status).toBe(409);
    expect(((await busy.json()) as { error: string }).error).toMatch(/still working/);

    release();
    await waitFor(async () => (await stopRequest(server).then((r) => r.status === 200 ? 'stopping' : null)));
    await waitFor(() => stops.length > 0);
    expect(stops).toEqual(['requested']);
  });

  it('sends open tabs the "stopped" close code', async () => {
    const { server } = await start();
    const t = tab(server);
    await t.open;
    expect((await stopRequest(server)).status).toBe(200);
    expect(await t.closed).toBe(STOPPED_CLOSE_CODE);
  });

  it('needs the token to stop', async () => {
    const { server, stops } = await start();
    expect((await fetch(`${server.url}/api/stop`, { method: 'POST' })).status).toBe(401);
    expect(stops).toEqual([]);
  });
});

# Claude in Chrome

Claude in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Claude in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Claude says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

If the only Claude in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Claude calls it first: it turns Claude in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.

## Loading the tools

If the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Claude loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:

```
ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"
```

Claude adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.

## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab

At the start of each browser session Claude calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:

1. Claude reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.
2. Otherwise Claude opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.
3. Claude never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Claude calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.

## Site permissions

Claude in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Claude tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Claude moves on.

## Recording a GIF

For multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Claude can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Claude captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example "login_process.gif").

## Reading console output

`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Claude is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern "[MyApp]" to keep only the application's own logs.

## Alerts and dialogs

Claude does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:

1. Claude avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a "Delete" button) unless necessary.
2. If it must interact with such an element, Claude warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.
3. Claude can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.

If a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Claude tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.

## Staying on task, and when to stop

Claude stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Claude stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:

- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts
- the extension gives no response
- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out
- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents
- several approaches have not completed the task

Claude does not keep retrying the same failing action.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-03 22:33:12Z)**_

Both are done. Auto-open already worked; I just hadn't used it. Auto-close is now built.

**Auto-open:** `codemap` already opens the map in your browser by default. I turned that off with `--no-open` on the last two runs, and the skill told agents to hand you a link instead. The skill now says to let it open the tab, and to share the link only as a backup.

**Auto-close:**
- **Closing the tab:** the server stops about 30 seconds after the last codemap tab closes. The 30 seconds lets a page reload reconnect without the server stopping.
- **Never mid-job:** it doesn't stop while Claude is working, so a map you closed early still finishes and gets saved first.
- **No tab ever opened:** it waits 10 minutes, then stops.
- **"Stop codemap" button:** on the map toolbar and at the bottom of the home page. It's greyed out while Claude is working, and the server also refuses a stop request then.
- **After it stops:** open tabs show "codemap has stopped" and how to reopen your maps, instead of trying to reconnect forever. That also happens after Ctrl+C.

**What I checked:**
- 7 new tests cover the rules above (stops after the last tab, survives a reload, waits for Claude, the button and its refusal mid-job, the token check). All 109 tests pass, typecheck is clean, and the viewer is rebuilt.
- I ran the real CLI with a test connection standing in for a tab. It exited 31 seconds after the connection closed and printed "No codemap tab is open, so codemap stopped."
- I couldn't check the button or the "stopped" screen in a browser, because the Chrome extension wasn't connected. To try it yourself: run `codemap open --repo .`, then press "Stop codemap" or close the tab.

**One trade-off:** answers in the side panel and the Undo for an applied fix live only in server memory, so they're lost when the server stops. That was already true on restart; now it happens every time you close the tab. The button's tooltip says so. Saving those answers is already on the `HANDOFF.md` to-do list, and this makes it more urgent.

I also updated the README and `CLAUDE.md`. Nothing is committed yet.

/** Fix states for answers' proposals. `known` is the server's view (on load); new answers' fixes start as proposed. */
function fixesFrom(answers: Answer[], prev: Record<string, FixState>, known: MapPayload['fixes'] | undefined): Record<string, FixState> {
  const out = { ...prev };
  for (const a of answers) {
    if (!a.fix || (out[a.fix.id] && !known)) continue;
    const k = known ? known[a.fix.id] : { status: 'proposed' as const };
    out[a.fix.id] = { proposal: a.fix, answerId: a.id, status: k?.status ?? 'rejected', problems: [], edgeId: k?.edgeId ?? null, closed: k?.closed ?? [] };
  }
  return out;
}

export function reducer(s: State, a: Action): State {
  switch (a.type) {
    case 'loaded': {
      const p = a.payload;
      const phase = p.map ? 'ready' : p.job ? 'making' : p.failure ? 'failed' : 'missing';
      return {
        ...s,
        phase,
        meta: p.meta,
        map: p.map,
        report: p.report,
        job: p.job,
        error: p.failure?.error ?? null,
        answers: p.answers,
        shown: p.answers.at(-1)?.id ?? null,
        fixes: fixesFrom(p.answers, s.fixes, p.fixes ?? {}),
      };
    }
    case 'missing':
      return { ...s, phase: 'missing' };
    case 'connected':
      return { ...s, connected: a.value };
    case 'event': {
      const e = a.event;
      if (e.mapId !== s.mapId) return s;
      if (e.type === 'job') {
        if (e.status === 'started') return { ...s, job: { kind: e.job, question: e.question, progress: [] }, error: null, phase: e.job === 'make' ? 'making' : s.phase };
        if (e.status === 'failed') return { ...s, job: null, error: e.error ?? 'Something went wrong.', phase: e.job === 'make' && !s.map ? 'failed' : s.phase };
        return { ...s, job: null };
      }
      if (e.type === 'progress') return s.job ? { ...s, job: { ...s.job, progress: [...s.job.progress, e.text].slice(-200) } } : s;
      if (e.type === 'map') {
        const keep = (ids: string[]) => ids.filter((id) => e.map.nodes.some((n) => n.id === id) || e.map.edges.some((x) => x.id === id) || e.map.absences.some((x) => x.id === id));
        const selection = { nodes: keep(s.selection.nodes), edges: keep(s.selection.edges), absences: keep(s.selection.absences) };
        return { ...s, phase: 'ready', meta: e.meta, map: e.map, report: e.report, selection };
      }
      if (e.type === 'answer') {
        const answers = [...s.answers, e.answer];
        const next: State = { ...s, answers, shown: e.answer.id, tour: null, depth: 'concept', fresh: e.answer.added, fixes: fixesFrom([e.answer], s.fixes, undefined) };
        const ids = [...e.answer.moves.highlight, ...e.answer.added];
        const highlight = s.map ? [...new Set([...ids, ...edgesWithin(s.map, new Set(ids))])] : ids;
        return highlight.length || e.answer.moves.focus ? pushView(next, { focus: e.answer.moves.focus ?? highlight[0] ?? null, highlight }) : next;
      }
      if (e.type === 'fix') {
        const f = s.fixes[e.fixId];
        if (!f) return s;
        const status: FixState['status'] = e.status;
        const fixes = { ...s.fixes, [e.fixId]: { ...f, status, problems: e.problems ?? [], edgeId: e.edgeId ?? f.edgeId, closed: e.closed ?? f.closed } };
        const next = { ...s, fixes };
        if (e.status === 'applied' && e.edgeId) {
          const c = f.proposal.connects;
          return pushView(next, { focus: e.edgeId, highlight: [e.edgeId, ...(c ? [c.from, c.to] : [])] });
        }
        return next;
      }
      return s;
    }
    case 'select': {
      const list = s.selection[a.kind];
      const has = list.includes(a.id);
      const selection = a.additive
        ? { ...s.selection, [a.kind]: has ? list.filter((x) => x !== a.id) : [...list, a.id] }
        : { ...emptySel(), [a.kind]: has && selSize(s.selection) === 1 ? [] : [a.id] };
      return { ...s, selection };
    }
    case 'selectMany':
      return { ...s, selection: a.selection };
    case 'clearSelection':
      return { ...s, selection: emptySel() };
    case 'tour': {
      if (a.stop === null || !s.map) return { ...s, tour: null };
      const stop = Math.max(0, Math.min(a.stop, s.map.tour.length - 1));
      return pushView({ ...s, tour: stop, selection: emptySel() }, stopView(s.map, stop));
    }
    case 'focus': {
      if (!s.map) return s;
      const kind: keyof Sel | null = s.map.nodes.some((n) => n.id === a.id) ? 'nodes' : s.map.edges.some((e) => e.id === a.id) ? 'edges' : s.map.absences.some((x) => x.id === a.id) ? 'absences' : null;
      if (!kind) return s;
      return pushView({ ...s, tour: null, selection: { ...emptySel(), [kind]: [a.id] } }, { focus: a.id, highlight: [a.id] });
    }
    case 'back':
      return s.viewIndex > 0 ? { ...s, viewIndex: s.viewIndex - 1 } : s.viewIndex === 0 ? { ...s, viewIndex: -1 } : s;
    case 'forward':
      return s.viewIndex < s.views.length - 1 ? { ...s, viewIndex: s.viewIndex + 1 } : s;
    case 'depth':
      return { ...s, depth: a.depth };
    case 'show':
      return { ...s, shown: a.answerId };
    case 'fixStatus': {
      const f = s.fixes[a.fixId];
      return f ? { ...s, fixes: { ...s.fixes, [a.fixId]: { ...f, status: a.status, problems: a.problems ?? f.problems } } } : s;
    }
    case 'error':
      return { ...s, error: a.message };
  }
}

// The input bar floating over the map. What's selected rides along as chips; Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { nameOf } from './panel';
import type { Sel } from './state';
import type { CodeMap } from './types';

export type ComposerProps = {
  map: CodeMap;
  selection: Sel;
  draft: string;
  busy: boolean;
  onDraft: (text: string) => void;
  onRemove: (kind: keyof Sel, id: string) => void;
  onSend: () => void;
};

export function Composer({ map, selection, draft, busy, onDraft, onRemove, onSend }: ComposerProps) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement>(null);
  const chips = (['nodes', 'edges', 'absences'] as const).flatMap((kind) => selection[kind].map((id) => ({ kind, id })));

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = ref.current;
    if (!el) return;
    el.style.height = 'auto';
    el.style.height = `${Math.min(el.scrollHeight, 140)}px`;
  }, [draft]);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (draft) ref.current?.focus();
  }, [draft === '']);

  return (
    <form
      className="composer"
      onSubmit={(e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        if (!busy && draft.trim()) onSend();
      }}
    >
      {chips.map((c) => (
        <span key={`${c.kind}:${c.id}`} className={`sel-chip sel-${c.kind}`}>
          <span className="sel-text" title={nameOf(map, c.id)}>
            {c.kind === 'absences' ? '✕ ' : '◉ '}
            {nameOf(map, c.id)}
          </span>
          <button type="button" aria-label={`Remove ${nameOf(map, c.id)}`} onClick={() => onRemove(c.kind, c.id)}>×</button>
        </span>
      ))}
      <textarea
        ref={ref}
        id="ask"
        rows={1}
        value={draft}
        placeholder={busy ? 'Claude is working…' : chips.length ? 'Ask about what you selected…' : 'Ask about this map…'}
        onChange={(e) => onDraft(e.target.value)}
        onKeyDown={(e) => {
          if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) {
            e.preventDefault();
            if (!busy && draft.trim()) onSend();
          }
        }}
        aria-label="Ask a question about the map"
      />
      <button type="submit" className="send" disabled={busy || !draft.trim()} aria-label="Send">↑</button>
    </form>
  );
}

The walkthrough problem is partly a plain bug; the other two are design gaps. For each I've listed what's happening now in the code, options, and what I'd do.

## 1. Every question triggers a search

**Now:** every question starts a Claude session with file reading and searching turned on, and the instructions invite it to explore. Claude only sees the map plus the short quoted fragment for each box, so "how does X work" questions almost always send it into the code. The first follow-up also starts a new Claude session, so it doesn't remember any of the files it read while drawing the map.

**Options:**
- **(a) Answer from the map first.** A quick first pass with no file tools: just the map, plus the code a few lines around each cited line, gathered by plain code. It answers in a few seconds and says whether the map covered the question. If not, it moves on to a full search, shown as a visible "Looking in the code…" step, or offers a "Look in the code" button.
- **(b) Let you choose.** An "Explain" vs "Dig deeper" switch on the input bar. Simple, but you have to decide every time.
- **(c) Pick up the session that drew the map**, so Claude already knows what it read. That session is large, so every question would be expensive. I'd also need to check the Agent SDK docs before relying on how sessions resume or fork.

**What I'd do:** (a), moving on to a search automatically and showing that it did. It keeps simple questions cheap without asking you to decide every time.

## 2. You can't get back to the original walkthrough

**Now:** two things combine.
- **A bug:** once any answer exists, the "This map" card with "Take the walkthrough" never comes back. The side panel always shows the latest answer, and nothing in the viewer ever clears it. Only the small Walkthrough button in the top bar is left.
- **The map changes for good:** additions are merged into the saved map. The layout is redrawn, so boxes you already knew move, the NEW badges stay, and the walkthrough doesn't cover the new parts. The map as it was first drawn isn't kept anywhere.

**Options:**
- **(a) Quick fixes:** a close button on the answer card, Esc to return to the overview, and a "Whole map" button that clears the highlighting.
- **(b) Additions as layers:** the first map stays as the base, and each answer's additions become a layer you can show or hide, labeled with the question that added it ("+3 from 'where do rules run?'"). Hiding them all gives you the original map exactly. This needs each addition tagged with the answer that made it. That either goes in the map format, which should only change deliberately and with tests, or in the saved map's metadata.
- **(c) Keep the layout steady:** place new boxes without moving the ones already there.
- **(d) Let the walkthrough grow:** an answer that adds something also adds a "detour" stop, so the walkthrough tells the whole conversation.

**What I'd do:** (a) now, since it's small and fixes the bug; (b) next, with (c) alongside.

## 3. A different question means relaunching

**Now:** you don't need to relaunch. Clicking "codemap" at the top left goes to the home page, which has a "Map it" box, but nothing points you there. Meanwhile, a question typed on a map always grows that map. One of the "nothing does X" claims on the third map was exactly that: asking never starts a new map. So a question about an unrelated part gets bolted on as a separate area.

**Options:**
- **(a) Claude says when it's off-topic.** The quick first pass from section 1 also judges whether the question belongs to this map. If not, the answer card says "That's a different part of the app" with a "Make a new map for this" button, already filled in.
- **(b) A "New map" button and a map switcher** in the top bar, switching without reloading the page. That also keeps the connection open, so the server never stops in between.
- **(c) Linked maps:** a map made from a follow-up remembers where it came from, with breadcrumbs like "Patient converts › Nightly job". Boxes for the same function in two maps link to each other, so you can jump between them. Plain code can match those by function name, with no AI involved.
- **(d) One map of the whole repo** built up from every question. Bigger, and later.

**What I'd do:** (a) and (b) now, (c) later.

## Putting it together

All three fit one model: **one tab per repo, holding many maps, each with its own conversation.** Every question ends one of three ways, and the page always says which:
1. **A plain answer.** The map doesn't change; at most, parts of it are highlighted.
2. **New layer.** The new boxes are added to this map and can be hidden.
3. **A new map**, linked back to this one.

One thing comes first: answers live only in server memory today, and now they're lost every time the tab closes. History, layers and linked maps all need saved answers, so saving them should come first.

**Suggested order:**
1. Save answers to disk.
2. The walkthrough bug fix (2a).
3. Answer from the map first, including the off-topic check (1a with 3a).
4. Layers (2b).
5. The map switcher (3b).

Steps 1 and 2 are small, so I could build them now. Before step 3, decide one thing: when the map doesn't cover a question, should Claude go into the code on its own, or ask you first?

// Laying the map out with ELK, in two passes: each area's steps stack top to bottom in the order the arrows go, then
// the areas themselves run left to right along the arrows that cross between them. Missing connections and proposed
// fixes take part like arrows do. Arrows attach to the sides of the boxes that face each other.
import type { ElkExtendedEdge, ElkNode } from 'elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js';
import type { CodeMap } from './types';

export const NODE_W = 210;
export const NODE_H = 66;
export type Box = { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number };
/** Area boxes are absolute; node boxes are relative to their area. */
export type Layout = { areas: Record<string, Box>; nodes: Record<string, Box>; width: number; height: number };
export type ExtraEdge = { id: string; from: string; to: string };
export type Side = 't' | 'r' | 'b' | 'l';

// ELK is most of the bundle; load it on first layout so the page shell shows up first.
let elk: Promise<{ layout(graph: ElkNode): Promise<ElkNode> }> | null = null;
const getElk = () => (elk ??= import('elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js').then((m) => new m.default()));

const LAYERED = {
  'elk.algorithm': 'layered',
  'elk.layered.nodePlacement.strategy': 'NETWORK_SIMPLEX',
  'elk.layered.considerModelOrder.strategy': 'NODES_AND_EDGES',
};

/** Every connection on the map, as from → to pairs between boxes. */
function links(map: CodeMap, extra: readonly ExtraEdge[]): { id: string; from: string; to: string }[] {
  const ids = new Set(map.nodes.map((n) => n.id));
  return [
    ...map.edges.map((e) => ({ id: `e:${e.id}`, from: e.from, to: e.to })),
    ...map.absences.flatMap((a) => (a.between ? [{ id: `a:${a.id}`, from: a.between.from, to: a.between.to }] : [])),
    ...extra.map((x) => ({ id: `x:${x.id}`, from: x.from, to: x.to })),
  ].filter((l) => ids.has(l.from) && ids.has(l.to) && l.from !== l.to);
}

export async function layoutMap(map: CodeMap, extra: readonly ExtraEdge[] = []): Promise<Layout> {
  const engine = await getElk();
  const areaOf = new Map(map.nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n.area]));
  const all = links(map, extra);

  // Pass 1: each area on its own, top to bottom, with room between rows for arrow labels.
  const nodes: Record<string, Box> = {};
  const sizes: Record<string, { w: number; h: number }> = {};
  for (const area of map.areas) {
    const members = map.nodes.filter((n) => n.area === area.id);
    if (!members.length) continue;
    const inside = all.filter((l) => areaOf.get(l.from) === area.id && areaOf.get(l.to) === area.id);
    const out = await engine.layout({
      id: area.id,
      layoutOptions: {
        ...LAYERED,
        'elk.direction': 'DOWN',
        'elk.padding': '[top=46,left=22,bottom=22,right=22]',
        'elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers': '56',
        'elk.spacing.nodeNode': '36',
      },
      children: members.map((n) => ({ id: n.id, width: NODE_W, height: NODE_H })),
      edges: inside.map((l): ElkExtendedEdge => ({ id: l.id, sources: [l.from], targets: [l.to] })),
    });
    for (const c of out.children ?? []) nodes[c.id] = { x: c.x ?? 0, y: c.y ?? 0, w: NODE_W, h: NODE_H };
    sizes[area.id] = { w: out.width ?? NODE_W + 44, h: out.height ?? NODE_H + 68 };
  }

  // Pass 2: the areas, left to right, joined by the arrows that cross between them (one per pair is enough).
  const pairs = new Map<string, { from: string; to: string }>();
  for (const l of all) {
    const from = areaOf.get(l.from)!;
    const to = areaOf.get(l.to)!;
    if (from !== to && sizes[from] && sizes[to]) pairs.set(`${from}>${to}`, { from, to });
  }
  const out = await engine.layout({
    id: 'root',
    layoutOptions: { ...LAYERED, 'elk.direction': 'RIGHT', 'elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers': '120', 'elk.spacing.nodeNode': '48', 'elk.spacing.componentComponent': '64' },
    children: map.areas.filter((a) => sizes[a.id]).map((a) => ({ id: a.id, width: sizes[a.id]!.w, height: sizes[a.id]!.h })),
    edges: [...pairs.values()].map((p, i): ElkExtendedEdge => ({ id: `p${i}`, sources: [p.from], targets: [p.to] })),
  });
  const areas: Record<string, Box> = {};
  for (const c of out.children ?? []) areas[c.id] = { x: c.x ?? 0, y: c.y ?? 0, w: c.width ?? 0, h: c.height ?? 0 };
  return { areas, nodes, width: out.width ?? 0, height: out.height ?? 0 };
}

/** Which sides an arrow leaves and enters by: down within an area, across between areas side by side. */
export function sides(map: CodeMap, layout: Layout, from: string, to: string): [Side, Side] {
  const areaOf = (id: string) => map.nodes.find((n) => n.id === id)?.area ?? '';
  const abs = (id: string) => {
    const a = layout.areas[areaOf(id)];
    const n = layout.nodes[id];
    return a && n ? { x: a.x + n.x + n.w / 2, y: a.y + n.y + n.h / 2 } : { x: 0, y: 0 };
  };
  const p = abs(from);
  const q = abs(to);
  const dx = q.x - p.x;
  const dy = q.y - p.y;
  if (areaOf(from) === areaOf(to) || Math.abs(dx) < NODE_W * 0.75) return dy >= 0 ? ['b', 't'] : ['t', 'b'];
  return dx >= 0 ? ['r', 'l'] : ['l', 'r'];
}

/** A key that changes only when the layout would: which boxes exist, where they live, and what connects them. */
export function layoutKey(map: CodeMap, extra: readonly ExtraEdge[] = []): string {
  return JSON.stringify([
    map.areas.map((a) => a.id),
    map.nodes.map((n) => `${n.id}@${n.area}`),
    map.edges.map((e) => `${e.from}>${e.to}`),
    map.absences.map((a) => (a.between ? `${a.between.from}~${a.between.to}` : '')),
    extra.map((x) => `${x.from}+${x.to}`),
  ]);
}
// Answering a question about a map. Claude starts from the map and explores the repo when it isn't enough. Anything it
// adds must pass the checker or it isn't drawn; a requested change comes back as a validated fix proposal, never an edit.
import * as crypto from 'node:crypto';
import { addToMap, check, mapIds, parseMap, type CheckReport, type CodeMap } from '@codemap/core';
import type { Agent, Progress } from './agent';
import { proposeFix, type FixProposal } from './fixes';
import { explainerPrompt, type SelectionLine } from './prompts';
import { ANSWER_SCHEMA, RawAnswer } from './schemas';

export type Selection = { nodes?: string[]; edges?: string[]; absences?: string[] };
export type RefStatus = { id: string; status: 'confirmed' | 'unconfirmed' | 'unknown' };
export type Answer = {
  id: string;
  question: string;
  selection: Selection;
  concept: string;
  how: string;
  code: string;
  refs: RefStatus[];
  followUps: string[];
  moves: { focus: string | null; highlight: string[] };
  /** Ids drawn on the map because of this answer (all confirmed). */
  added: string[];
  /** What was found but not drawn, and why; problems with a proposed fix. */
  problems: string[];
  fix: FixProposal | null;
  cost: number;
};
export type AnswerOptions = {
  root: string;
  map: CodeMap;
  selection: Selection;
  question: string;
  agent: Agent;
  session: string | null;
  model?: string;
  onProgress?: (p: Progress) => void;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
};

function selectionLines(map: CodeMap, s: Selection): SelectionLine[] {
  const nodes = new Map(map.nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n]));
  const label = (id: string) => nodes.get(id)?.name ?? id;
  return [
    ...(s.nodes ?? []).filter((id) => nodes.has(id)).map((id) => ({ id, label: `box "${label(id)}"` })),
    ...(s.edges ?? []).flatMap((id) => {
      const e = map.edges.find((x) => x.id === id);
      return e ? [{ id, label: `arrow "${e.label}" from "${label(e.from)}" to "${label(e.to)}"` }] : [];
    }),
    ...(s.absences ?? []).flatMap((id) => {
      const a = map.absences.find((x) => x.id === id);
      return a ? [{ id, label: `missing connection: ${a.claim}` }] : [];
    }),
  ];
}

/** The map without the given ids (and without arrows or tour mentions that point at removed boxes). */
function without(map: CodeMap, ids: ReadonlySet<string>): CodeMap {
  const nodes = map.nodes.filter((n) => !ids.has(n.id));
  const kept = new Set(nodes.map((n) => n.id));
// What the model must return, as JSON Schema for structured output. Derived from the map format's zod schemas, so the
// two can't drift. Output is still validated with zod (and the map with `parseMap`) after it comes back.
import { z } from 'zod';
import { Absence, Area, CodeMap, Edge, Node } from '@codemap/core';

/** Keywords some structured-output validators reject; zod and `parseMap` enforce them after the fact anyway. */
const STRIP = new Set(['$schema', '$id', 'pattern', 'default', 'format']);

function sanitize(value: unknown): unknown {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(sanitize);
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return value;
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(value)) if (!STRIP.has(k)) out[k] = sanitize(v);
  return out;
}

export function toSchema(schema: z.ZodType): Record<string, unknown> {
  return sanitize(z.toJSONSchema(schema, { io: 'input' })) as Record<string, unknown>;
}

export const RawFix = z.object({
  summary: z.string().min(1).max(600),
  /** Exact-text replacements: `find` is copied from the file and occurs exactly once. */
  edits: z.array(z.object({ file: z.string().min(1), find: z.string().min(1), replace: z.string() })).max(12).default([]),
  creates: z.array(z.object({ file: z.string().min(1), content: z.string() })).max(6).default([]),
  /** The connection the fix creates between two boxes; `evidenceText` must appear in the new code. */
  connects: z
    .object({ from: z.string(), to: z.string(), label: z.string().min(1).max(60), evidenceFile: z.string().min(1), evidenceText: z.string().min(1).max(200) })
    .optional(),
});

export const RawAnswer = z.object({
  concept: z.string().min(1),
  how: z.string().default(''),
  code: z.string().default(''),
  /** Ids of the boxes, arrows and missing connections the answer relies on. */
  refs: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
  /** New things found while exploring, with evidence, same rules as the map. */
  add: z
    .object({ areas: z.array(Area).optional(), nodes: z.array(Node).optional(), edges: z.array(Edge).optional(), absences: z.array(Absence).optional() })
      try {
        raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file(id), 'utf8'));
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
      const parsed = parseMap(raw.map);
      return parsed.ok && raw.meta ? { meta: raw.meta, map: parsed.map } : null;
    },
    save(stored: StoredMap): void {
      ensure();
      const target = file(stored.meta.id);
      const tmp = `${target}.tmp`;
      fs.writeFileSync(tmp, `${JSON.stringify(stored, null, 2)}\n`);
      fs.renameSync(tmp, target);
    },
    list(): MapMeta[] {
      if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) return [];
      return fs
        .readdirSync(dir)
        .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.json'))
        .flatMap((f) => {
          try {
            const meta = (JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, f), 'utf8')) as { meta?: MapMeta }).meta;
            return meta ? [meta] : [];
          } catch {
            return [];
          }
        })
        .sort((a, b) => b.updatedAt.localeCompare(a.updatedAt));
    },
    /** A new id for a question, unique among saved maps and ids already handed out. */
    newId(question: string, taken: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set()): string {
      const base = slugify(question);
      for (let i = 1; ; i++) {
        const id = i === 1 ? base : `${base}-${i}`;
        if (!taken.has(id) && !fs.existsSync(file(id))) return id;
      }
    },
  };
}

const EXCERPT_RADIUS = 4;
const MAX_EXCERPTS = 40;
const MAX_EXCERPT_CHARS = 30_000;

/**
 * The code around each line the map cites, read through the secret-refusing reader: what the selection cites first,
 * then the rest of the map, until the budget runs out. Plain code, no model.
 */
export function citedExcerpts(root: string, map: CodeMap, selection: Selection): string {
  const repo = createRepoReader(root);
  const picked = new Set([...(selection.nodes ?? []), ...(selection.edges ?? [])]);
  const items = [...map.nodes.map((n) => ({ id: n.id, evidence: n.evidence })), ...map.edges.map((e) => ({ id: e.id, evidence: e.evidence }))];
  items.sort((a, b) => Number(picked.has(b.id)) - Number(picked.has(a.id)));
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const out: string[] = [];
  let size = 0;
  for (const item of items) {
    for (const e of item.evidence) {
      const key = `${e.file}:${e.line}`;
      if (seen.has(key) || out.length >= MAX_EXCERPTS) continue;
      seen.add(key);
      const read = repo.read(e.file);
      if (!read.ok) continue;
      const lines = read.text.split('\\n');
      const from = Math.max(1, e.line - EXCERPT_RADIUS);
      const to = Math.min(lines.length, e.line + EXCERPT_RADIUS);
      const body = lines.slice(from - 1, to).map((l, i) => `${String(from + i).padStart(5)} | ${l}`).join('\\n');
      const block = `${e.file}:${from}-${to} (cited by ${item.id})\\n${body}`;
      if (size + block.length > MAX_EXCERPT_CHARS) return out.join('\\n\\n');
      out.push(block);
      size += block.length;
    }
  }
  return out.join('\\n\\n');
}""")

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-03 22:50:03Z)**_

I didn't touch any files, since the other agent is editing. I timed the three map sessions from today using their saved transcripts, and the result changes the plan: on this repo, exploring isn't where the time goes.

| Part of making a map | Seconds (of roughly 105–125) |
|---|---|
| Exploring (Claude's turns that read and search) | 13–22 |
| Thinking between steps | 12–32 |
| **Writing the map** | **~40** |
| **Repair round: rewriting the whole map** | **~36** |
| Running the reads and searches, the scan and the checker | ~1 |

About 70% of the time goes to writing the map, and in all three runs Claude wrote it twice. That also corrects something I told you earlier: the drafting-loop map did not pass on its first round. Its first draft failed 3 claims, all over function names. Claude cited `server.ts#startMap` and `store.ts#save`, but the scanner doesn't record either one: functions defined inside other functions aren't indexed, so `startMap` only shows up as `CodemapServer.startMap`. The repair round then rewrote all 10 boxes and 11 arrows to fix 3 citations.

A Graphify-style graph would mostly speed up the 13–22 seconds of exploring. It's still the right long-term direction, because exploring is what grows on big repos and writing the map doesn't. But it won't fix the two minutes you're seeing now.

## What I'd do, in order
1. **Repairs as patches.** Ask Claude for replacements for just the failed claims, not "the complete corrected map". That should cut roughly 30 seconds from most maps. It's small, and only touches `prompts.ts`, `maker.ts` and a schema.
2. **Give Claude the exact function names up front.** Put the scanner's real symbol ids, with their line numbers, into the prompt for the files it's likely to cite, so the first draft passes. Also index functions defined inside other functions, which is the gap that caused today's failures. This is the first slice of your graph idea, and it removes the cause of most repairs.
3. **Draw the boxes first, write the prose after.** Return areas, boxes and arrows quickly, show them, then write the three-depth explanations and the walkthrough in a second call. The "code" depth is mostly function and file names, which plain code could fill in.
4. **Then the persistent graph**, below.

## On the graph itself

**Don't pull in Graphify.** We already have most of what it does: `@codemap/facts` extracts imports, symbols, calls, routes, table writes and which requests hit which routes. Graphify doesn't link requests to routes or track events for JS, which `HANDOFF.md` lists as codemap's advantage. The gap is that we throw our scan away after every map: Claude only sees about 40 summary lines from it, and the checker re-extracts facts each time. The ideas worth borrowing are the ones `HANDOFF.md` already lists:
- every connection belongs to the file it came from
- a connection only counts with import evidence
- group ids stay stable between rebuilds
- the graph is stamped with the commit it was built from

**What changes for Claude:** plain code picks the part of the graph that matters for the question, by matching the question's words to function names and following connections a couple of steps out. Claude gets that, with exact names and lines, and its main job becomes what you described: choosing, naming, grouping into areas, and finding gaps. It can still search the code when the graph isn't enough.

Keyword matching is Graphify's weak spot, so Claude should keep its search tools. Giving it a "query the graph" tool would need a custom tool through the Agent SDK. That would be a new kind of tool next to the three read-only ones in `agent.ts`, and the SDK docs need checking before relying on it.

**Keeping it fresh while code changes**, not just on push:
- **Per-file cache:** store `.codemap/index/` (gitignored) holding, per file, a hash of its contents plus the facts extracted from it. The scanner already extracts facts one file at a time, so this fits.
- **Check freshness on every use:** before each map, answer or check, compare file timestamps and sizes, and re-extract only the files that changed. That keeps the graph correct even if the watcher below misses something.
- **Update only what a change touches:** when a file changes, drop its own connections and redo just the cross-file links that depend on it, using a reverse import index.
- **Watch for edits while codemap is open:** Node's file watcher catches any editor or agent, debounced so a branch switch is handled as one burst. On a change, re-check the open map, so claims flip to "?" as soon as the code under them changes. That keeps the map honest while an agent is editing, and costs nothing because the checker never calls a model.

Claude Code hooks could also tell codemap exactly which files an agent edited, but a watcher already covers every editor and agent, so I'd skip hooks unless the watcher turns out to be unreliable.

**Caveats:**
- This repo is small, about 3,400 lines of source. On a big repo exploring grows and the graph pays off more, but the first full scan there is also untested.
- Answers took 18–30 seconds each, again mostly writing.

Once the other agent's changes land, I'd start with steps 1 and 2. They're independent of its work and should show up in the next map you make.

// ELK layout of the care-app map: steps stack down inside their area, areas run left to right along the arrows, every
// box stays inside its area, and arrows attach to the sides that face each other.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { parseMap } from '@codemap/core';
import { layoutKey, layoutMap, sides } from '../src/layout';

const map = (() => {
  const r = parseMap(JSON.parse(readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('../../core/test/fixtures/care-app.map.json', import.meta.url)), 'utf8')));
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(r.problems.join('\n'));
  return r.map;
})();

describe('layoutMap', () => {
  it('places every box inside its area, and every area', async () => {
    const l = await layoutMap(map);
    expect(Object.keys(l.areas).sort()).toEqual(['automations', 'events', 'jobs', 'patients']);
    for (const n of map.nodes) {
      const box = l.nodes[n.id]!;
      const area = l.areas[n.area]!;
      expect(box.x).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
      expect(box.y).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
      expect(box.x + box.w).toBeLessThanOrEqual(area.w);
      expect(box.y + box.h).toBeLessThanOrEqual(area.h);
    }
  });

  it('stacks steps down inside an area, and runs areas left to right along the path', async () => {
    const l = await layoutMap(map);
    expect(l.nodes.s1!.y).toBeLessThan(l.nodes.s2!.y);
    expect(l.nodes.s2!.y).toBeLessThan(l.nodes.s3!.y);
    expect(l.nodes.u1!.y).toBeLessThan(l.nodes.u3!.y);
    expect(l.areas.patients!.x).toBeLessThan(l.areas.events!.x);
    expect(l.areas.events!.x).toBeLessThan(l.areas.automations!.x); // the missing connection still pulls Automations right
    expect(l.areas.jobs!.x).toBeLessThan(l.areas.automations!.x);
  });

  it('attaches arrows to facing sides: down within an area, across between areas', async () => {
    const l = await layoutMap(map);
    expect(sides(map, l, 's1', 's2')).toEqual(['b', 't']);
    expect(sides(map, l, 's3', 's4')).toEqual(['r', 'l']);
    expect(sides(map, l, 'j1', 'u1')).toEqual(['r', 'l']);
  });

  it('changes its key only when the structure changes', () => {
    const renamed = { ...map, nodes: map.nodes.map((n) => (n.id === 's1' ? { ...n, name: 'Different words' } : n)) };
    expect(layoutKey(renamed)).toBe(layoutKey(map));
    expect(layoutKey(map, [{ id: 'fix-1', from: 's4', to: 'u1' }])).not.toBe(layoutKey(map));
  });
});

async function layoutArea(engine: Engine, areaId: string, members: readonly { id: string }[], inside: readonly { id: string; from: string; to: string }[]) {

/** What each answer added that is still on the map: the layers someone can show or hide. */
export function layersOf(s: State): { answerId: string; question: string; ids: string[]; visible: boolean }[] {
  if (!s.map) return [];
  const live = new Set([...s.map.areas, ...s.map.nodes, ...s.map.edges, ...s.map.absences].map((x) => x.id));
  return s.answers.flatMap((a) => {
    const ids = a.added.filter((id) => live.has(id));
    return ids.length ? [{ answerId: a.id, question: a.question, ids, visible: !s.hidden.includes(a.id) }] : [];
  });
}

/** Everything answers added (shown or not): the layout keeps the original map's boxes in place around these. */
export const addedIds = (s: State): string[] => layersOf(s).flatMap((l) => l.ids);

/** The map as drawn: without hidden layers, or arrows and gaps that lost an end. */
export function visibleMap(s: State): CodeMap | null {
  if (!s.map) return null;
  const hide = new Set(layersOf(s).filter((l) => !l.visible).flatMap((l) => l.ids));
  if (!hide.size) return s.map;
  const nodes = s.map.nodes.filter((n) => !hide.has(n.id));
  const kept = new Set(nodes.map((n) => n.id));
  return {
    ...s.map,
    areas: s.map.areas.filter((a) => !hide.has(a.id)),
    nodes,
    edges: s.map.edges.filter((e) => !hide.has(e.id) && kept.has(e.from) && kept.has(e.to)),
    absences: s.map.absences.filter((a) => !hide.has(a.id) && (!a.between || (kept.has(a.between.from) && kept.has(a.between.to)))),
  };
}

/** The selection, minus anything not drawn. */
function keepDrawn(selection: Sel, map: CodeMap | null): Sel {
  if (!map) return selection;
  const on = (ids: string[], list: readonly { id: string }[]) => ids.filter((id) => list.some((x) => x.id === id));
  return { nodes: on(selection.nodes, map.nodes), edges: on(selection.edges, map.edges), absences: on(selection.absences, map.absences) };
}""")

import { db } from '../db';
import { evaluateRules } from '../automations/evaluate';

// Runs at 2:00 am, for patients created the day before.
export const schedule = '0 2 * * *';

export async function runNightly() {
  const yesterday = new Date(Date.now() - 86_400_000);
  const patients = await db.where('patients', { createdAfter: yesterday });
  for (const patient of patients) await evaluateRules({ patientId: patient.id });
}
import { db } from '../db';
import { queueEmail } from '../jobs/queue';

export async function evaluateRules({ patientId }: { patientId: string }) {
  const rules = await db.where('automation_rules', { trigger: 'converted' });
  for (const rule of rules) if (rule.action === 'welcome_email') await queueEmail(patientId, rule.template);
}

Sections 1 and 2 are built. All 116 tests pass (14 of them new), typecheck is clean and the viewer is rebuilt. I also asked three real questions on a copy of the care-app test project.

## 1. Simple questions are answered from the map
- **Map first:** every question first goes to Claude with no file tools, just the map plus the code a few lines around each line it cites. Plain code gathers those lines, never from secret files, starting with whatever you selected.
- **Then the code, only if needed:** if Claude says the map isn't enough, the question goes on to the full search, with a note on what was missing so the search starts in the right place. The panel shows "Claude is looking in the code" when that happens.
- **Only the full search changes anything:** the map-only step can't add to the map or propose a fix.
- **Each answer is labeled** "from the map" or "looked in the code".

The real runs:

| Question | Answered | Time | API-price estimate |
|---|---|---|---|
| What does this step do? (one box selected) | from the map | ~15 s | |
| Which patients does the nightly job pick? | from the map | 15 s | $0.07 |
| Is the database real? (a file the map doesn't cite) | in the code, after the map-only try said no | 30 s | $0.13 |

I checked both last answers against the code and they're right. The third one added 6 checked items to the map. The cost figures are API-price estimates, not charges to you.

## 2. Getting back to the original map and walkthrough
- **The bug is fixed:** answers have a close button (×), there's a "Whole map" button in the toolbar, and Esc steps back one level at a time: walkthrough, then selection, then the answer. The overview card with "Take the walkthrough" comes back each time.
- **Reopened maps** start at the overview instead of the last answer.
- **Layers:** a panel card, "Added by your questions", lists each answer that added to the map, labeled with its question and a count. Each has a checkbox, plus a "Show the original map" button.
- **Steady layout:** the map as first drawn is laid out on its own, then additions are fitted around it. Additions to an existing area go in rows below its boxes; new areas go to the right. Original boxes never move, though an area below one that grew can slide down. A test checks this.

## Saving answers (needed for layers)
Questions, answers and where each fix stands are now saved in the map file, so they survive a restart and the tab closing. Undo is the exception: it needs the files as they were before the fix, which only the running server holds. After a restart, the fix card says to use git instead.

**Not checked:** I haven't seen any of the new screens in a browser, since the Chrome extension wasn't connected. That covers the Stop button and "stopped" screen from earlier too. `npm run preview` now shows a map-only answer for "what does this do?", if you want a quick look.

Nothing is committed yet: 26 changed files, plus `stop.tsx` and `stop.test.ts`. I updated `CLAUDE.md` and `HANDOFF.md` to match.
